text:
Sjoe! The Unfinished Negotiation 🌍  Has Reached Washington ~ 🧮🇿🇦 When 300,141 Members Become a “Small Minority” ~ 🎙️ The Ambassador Said “Small.” The Membership Forms Said Otherwise.
South Africa’s ambassador to the United States, Roelf Meyer, examined organisations that report more than 300 000 members for AfriForum and more than 600 000 across the Solidarity Movement, then described them as a “small minority.”

The numbers did not cooperate.

AfriForum’s May 2026 records list 300 141 members: 261 973 monthly contributors, 5 639 annual contributors, and 32 799 non-contributing members. The Solidarity Movement places its combined reach above 600 000. Statistics South Africa’s mid-year estimates put the white population at 4.521 million, or 7.1 percent of 63.52 million South Africans. 

Against that base the fee-paying ranks already form a measurable organised share. Meyer linked the critics to the 30 percent who voted “No” in the 1992 white referendum. The organisations answered with membership lists that expanded while the demographic base contracted. 

The gap between the adjective and the ledger is the story.

1. The Numbers That Refuse to Be Small

In the early 2000s AfriForum counted members in the low thousands. By 2026 the figure exceeded 300 000. Solidarity’s affiliated structures report hundreds of thousands more. This growth occurred while the white population fell from roughly 5.2 million in the mid-1990s to 4.521 million, a net loss driven largely by emigration (Statistics South Africa, 2026).

The arithmetic is stubborn. 

A constituency that expands as its demographic pool shrinks is not performing residual politics. It is responding to present conditions. Those members fund neighbourhood watches, legal teams, training centres and international offices. The resulting capacity sits alongside the state rather than inside it.

Constitutional democracy rests on the idea that organised citizens can speak without first seeking official permission for their size. When an ambassador’s description is smaller than the organisations’ own published rolls, the collision is not semantic. It is institutional. 

Representation claims that ignore the ledger eventually lose the ability to persuade anyone who can still count.

Sjoe!
It takes a special kind of diplomatic confidence to look at membership figures larger than the population of several mid-sized South African towns and still reach for the word “small.” The ledger, as usual, declined to play along.

Stirring Questions:
What does it mean when an official adjective is smaller than the organisations’ audited numbers? 
How should a democracy weigh self-reported membership against official minimisation? 
If the numbers continue rising while the population share falls, what does that trajectory reveal about the conditions producing the membership?

Taken together, these questions matter because they force a choice between rhetorical convenience and countable reality. A political order that cannot reconcile the two eventually finds its descriptions travelling alone.

2. Same Language, Opposite Maps

Roelf Meyer and Jaco Kleynhans both grew up speaking Afrikaans. Both come from rural or farming families. Both accept that the 1994 settlement is irreversible. From that shared ground they drew opposite maps.

Meyer rose through the Afrikaanse Studentebond and the National Party, served as the government’s chief negotiator opposite Cyril Ramaphosa, later joined the ANC, and now represents the state in Washington. He describes himself as an Afrikaner by heart but a South African first. He treats exclusive group institutions as a risk to national cohesion.

Kleynhans joined the Solidarity Movement’s communications work in the early 2000s and now leads its international liaison. He treats parallel education, safety structures and cultural institutions as practical necessities for a minority of roughly seven percent living under policies that still organise opportunity by race.

The same language produced two strategies. One defends the inclusive project from inside the state. The other builds capacity outside the state because it judges the inclusive project incomplete on safety, language and economic access. 

Political scientists have long noted that transitions produce both “settlement elites” who guard the original bargain and “post-settlement organisers” who measure the bargain against daily outcomes. South Africa’s Afrikaans-speaking community has generated both types in unusually clear form.

The disagreement is not about whether 1994 happened. It is about whether the settlement still requires minority self-organisation or whether that organisation itself threatens the settlement.

Sjoe!
One community, one language, two maps of the future, and an ambassador who has to explain the difference in Washington. History has a dry sense of humour.

Stirring Questions:
How does a community that shares language and history arrive at such different conclusions about survival inside the same constitutional order? 
When one generation negotiates the transition and the next organises the aftermath, whose experience carries more weight? 
If both men accept the irreversibility of 1994, what concrete outcomes would each accept as proof that the order is working?

These questions together expose a structural feature of the transition itself. The settlement produced both its most loyal institutional defenders and its most persistent external auditors. Understanding that split is necessary before anyone can claim to speak for the whole.

3. Growth Against the Grain

Between the mid-1990s and 2026 the white population declined by nearly 700 000 people. In the same window AfriForum’s membership multiplied many times and the Solidarity Movement expanded its institutional footprint. Organised affiliation moved in the opposite direction from demographic size.

People do not usually pay monthly fees to organisations whose relevance is fading. They join when they judge the organisations useful for present problems: farm and neighbourhood safety, employment equity outcomes, language rights, service delivery gaps. 

The consistency of the membership disclosures, matched by the visible growth of branches, watches and training programmes, supplies corroborating evidence of active choice (AfriForum, 2026; Kriel, 2026).Self-reported figures require caution. Yet when the same organisations publish detailed breakdowns year after year and those breakdowns track the expansion of concrete services, the data become harder to dismiss as marketing. 

The growth against demographic contraction turns membership numbers from a static claim into evidence of agency. Economists would recognise the pattern as revealed preference: scarce resources (time and money) allocated under real constraints.

Sjoe!
The population got smaller. The membership lists got longer. Somewhere an official narrative is still waiting for the numbers to catch up.

Stirring Questions:
If a population shrinks while its organised expression expands, what does that say about incentives inside the constitutional order? 
Can official characterisations of “small” survive repeated collisions with rising membership? 
When institutional capacity grows outside the state, does that strengthen or complicate the state’s claim to exclusive representation?

Together these questions point to a governance puzzle. Demographic decline without organisational decline forces a reckoning with why people continue to organise. Ignoring the pattern does not make it disappear; it only makes official descriptions look increasingly theatrical.

4. Exclusive or Inclusive — the Fault Line

Meyer has been consistent. He calls the approach of AfriForum and Solidarity “exclusive.” He argues that identity-based institutions, however successful on their own terms, ultimately fail the broader national project. 

The organisations reply that a minority of seven percent living under race-based legislation cannot rely solely on the inclusive ideal; it must also build its own schools, safety networks and legal capacity if it intends to remain.

The disagreement is prior to the statistics. It is a disagreement about what the 1994 settlement requires of a cultural and linguistic minority. One side treats exclusive organisation as a threat to non-racialism. The other treats the absence of such organisation as a guarantee of gradual erosion. 

Comparative politics offers parallel cases: minority communities in other divided societies have faced the same choice between trusting the state’s inclusive promise and constructing parallel capacity when that promise appears incomplete.

Once the fault line is recognised, the numbers and the demographic inversion become symptoms rather than the disease. The deeper argument is about whether the constitutional order still needs minority self-help or whether minority self-help itself undermines the order.

Sjoe!
The inclusive project and the exclusive institutions keep explaining each other to foreign audiences. Neither appears ready to leave the stage.

Stirring Questions:
Is an organisation that builds parallel capacity inside a constitutional democracy strengthening that democracy or preparing an exit from it? 
When the state continues to use race as a policy organising principle, what practical options remain for a minority that accepts the constitution but rejects the policy method? 
Can the same community produce both the most loyal defenders of the inclusive narrative and the most effective builders of exclusive capacity without the contradiction becoming permanent?

These questions together define the unfinished business of the transition. They ask whether non-racialism can coexist with race-based policy without generating permanent parallel institutions. 

The answer will shape more than one community’s future.

5. When Civil Society Opens Its Own Channel

Meyer’s appointment as ambassador was widely understood as an attempt to place an Afrikaner face in Washington to counter claims of minority persecution. At the same time Solidarity and AfriForum maintained their own sustained engagement with American and European institutions, presenting data on rural safety, race-based policy and trade instruments such as AGOA.

The result is dual-track diplomacy. 

The formal ambassador works to contain certain narratives. The civil-society organisations work to keep related concerns and economic interests visible. When non-state actors sometimes enjoy better access on specific files than the formal channel, the state’s monopoly on international representation is partially eroded. The internal disagreement has acquired an external dimension.

International relations scholarship has long examined “parallel diplomacy” by non-state actors. South Africa’s case is distinctive because the parallel channel and the formal channel emerge from the same cultural community and address the same foreign capitals with different diagnoses of the same society.

Sjoe!
One country, two sets of talking points, and foreign officials who must decide which ledger to trust. Diplomacy has rarely been this efficiently duplicated.

Stirring Questions:
What happens to a country’s foreign policy when its own civil society can open parallel doors in foreign capitals? 
Does the dual track strengthen South Africa’s overall voice or fracture it? 
If the ambassador and the organisations continue to present different pictures of the same society, which picture will foreign governments ultimately treat as more reliable?

Taken together, these questions turn a domestic argument about membership numbers into a question of national coherence on the international stage. The answers will affect trade access, investment perceptions, and the credibility of official narratives far beyond any single community.

What the Ledger Shows

The collision is not about arithmetic. It is about whether the post-1994 order still requires minority self-organisation or whether that organisation itself threatens the order. 

The same cultural community has produced both the state’s most credentialed defender of the inclusive narrative and the most effective parallel channel that questions the adequacy of that narrative.

The membership figures, the growth against demographic decline, the exclusive-versus-inclusive fault line, and the dual-track diplomacy are successive expressions of a single unresolved tension. 

The numbers will not shrink to fit the label. 
The maps of the future remain opposite. 
And Washington now hears from both.

South Africa has lived with difficult numbers before. The difference this time is that the numbers are organised, funded, and speaking in more than one capital at once. The ledger is public. The argument is structural. 

The country will have to decide what the ledger means.

Some U.S. schools and school districts have referred students (or provided on-site access) to organizations and clinics involved in gender-affirming care, including elements that can lead to medical interventions for minors. This is not universal—practices vary widely by district, state law, and year—and it is distinct from schools themselves performing surgeries or secretly transporting students for them (claims of the latter have been widely fact-checked as unsupported).⁠CNN

Documented examples of school involvement
Seattle Public Schools (Washington): School-based health centers at schools such as Nova High School and Meany Middle School (operated by Country Doctor Community Health Centers and previously linked to Neighborcare Health) have offered “gender-affirming” services. These included counseling, social identity support, hormone therapy (estrogen, testosterone, androgen blockers), and referrals for surgeries such as vaginoplasty or chest procedures. District statements noted that parental/guardian consent is required under Washington law for most services for minors under 18, and that the clinics are independently operated. Documents and emails from 2023 onward confirmed the expansion of these offerings.⁠Nationalreview⁠Dailywire⁠Defendinged
Newport Mesa Unified School District / Newport Harbor High School (California): Hallway QR codes and resources directed students to the LGBTQ Center of Orange County. That center’s materials included forms connecting minors to affirming therapists (who can provide referral letters for transition procedures) and doctors offering hormone regimens and gender-related surgeries. A proposed formal memorandum of understanding for counseling/referrals was withdrawn after parental pushback.⁠Dailysignal⁠Thepostmillennial
Multiple Wisconsin districts (including Madison Metropolitan, Janesville, Middleton-Cross Plains, Beloit, DeForest, and Monona Grove): These listed or provided UW Health’s PATH pediatric transgender clinic as a resource for students and families. The clinic offers puberty suppression, gender-affirming hormones, mental-health counseling, and related support.⁠Defendinged
Other districts have maintained resource lists, trained staff on social transition (names, pronouns, facilities), or partnered with local LGBTQ centers. Organizations such as GLSEN have long advocated for model school policies supporting social affirmation, nondiscrimination based on gender identity, and access to supportive resources; many districts have adopted elements of these approaches.

Biography
Early life
Sako was born in the city of Zakho, Iraq, on 4 July 1948.[3] He comes from an ethnic Assyrian family of the Chaldean Catholic Church that has roots in a religious community that has had a presence in the city of his birth since the 5th century AD.[4]

The footage, captured by a Ring camera at a residence in Virginia Beach on a Sunday afternoon, shows a delivery driver employed by GOFO approaching along a concrete path while carrying a white package. A large black cat (identified by the owner as Opie, a 21-pound short-hair) is resting motionless on the porch steps to the right. The driver advances to a short distance, executes an underhand throw that strikes the cat, then steps back, appears to smirk, photographs the package, and departs toward the waiting van. The cat had raised its head immediately before impact and was otherwise undisturbed.[](<https://t.co/GJlxrgcag7>)

Owner Isabell Sump described the animal as typically carefree and non-aggressive: it “wasn’t doing anything” when struck. She characterized the motion as deliberate—“an underhand throw and reared it back”—and noted the subsequent documentation of the scene. Sump has stated she intends to file criminal charges once the driver is identified, arguing that the act constitutes unnecessary harm and raises the possibility of a pattern. GOFO has contacted her, confirmed an internal investigation, and issued an apology. Some early social-media posts misidentified the vehicle or company as Amazon; local reporting and clarification establish the affiliation as GOFO.[](<https://t.co/GJlxrgcag7>)

The sequence leaves limited room for benign interpretation. The cat presented no obstacle or threat; the porch and steps offered ordinary placement options; and the post-throw reaction (smirk plus photograph) is consistent with intentional targeting rather than an accidental toss or reflexive startle. Plausible contributing factors include personal aversion to cats, residual Halloween-related superstition about black cats (explicitly noted by the owner), or simple amusement at the animal’s expense. None of these justify the action under ordinary delivery protocols. Delivery work involves time pressure and variable training, yet standard practice is to set packages down safely or leave them when an animal is present; intentional projectile use falls outside that range.

The incident illustrates several recurring frictions. First, doorbell and security cameras routinely document interactions between gig-economy workers and household pets; both positive (drivers pausing to pet cats) and negative examples circulate widely, shaping public expectations. Second, companies that rely on contracted or high-turnover drivers face heightened reputational exposure when footage of this kind appears, prompting rapid investigations even before formal identification. Third, Virginia animal-cruelty statutes can reach intentional acts that cause harm or distress; whether charges proceed depends on identification, evidence of injury or intent, and prosecutorial discretion. Fourth, viral amplification produces both accountability pressure and occasional misattribution, as seen in the initial Amazon labeling.

In practical terms, the owner’s suggested alternatives—leaving the package in the yard or simply walking away—align with ordinary caution. The footage itself supplies a clear record of the sequence, the animal’s passive posture, and the driver’s subsequent behavior, which local authorities and the employer can evaluate alongside any additional evidence the owner obtains.

***The 2026 Budget - what to expect***

FISCAL HEADROOM

* John Healey is expected to lower the fiscal headroom from £23bn to around £15bn after economic hit caused by Iran war

* Ministers fear fresh military strikes by the US against Iran in wake of mid-terms will render OBR forecasts obsolete within days - worse is to come

ENERGY BILLS

*Healey will extend the warm homes discount for families on benefits, giving them another £100 off their energy bills

* But households not on benefits will bear the full brunt of the rise in January, when bills are due to go up by 27% to an average of £2,192

* Gas standing charges will be scrapped next year, saving £27 on a typical bill although those with larger homes who use more energy will pay more

* Healey will announce long-term plans to move more green levies off energy bills in a bid to reduce them 'for good

* He's also expected to announce long-term plans to remove the link between gas prices and electricity prices

FUEL DUTY

* The fuel duty freeze - which was due to end in January - will be extended to help with soaring prices at the pumps

BANKING TAX

* The biggest 'revenue raiser' in the Budget. Healey has been lobbied to restore the 8% surcharge on corporation tax, which would raise £2bn

ONLINE RETAILER TAX

* Online retail giants like Amazon, eBay and Temu will be made responsible for collecting tax from retailers selling on their platforms

FAMILY BUSINESSES

* Thousands of high-street shops, cafes, pubs and hairdressers will no longer have to pay business rates. Move funded with online retailer tax

MINIMUM WAGE

* The living wage, paid by older workers, and the national minimum wage, paid by those aged 18 to 21, will increase by 3.9%. Healey has chosen to stop the huge rises in the minimum wage amid concerns it was pricing young people out of work

PENSIONERS

* Healey will announce plans to shield 1million pensioners from paying income tax

* The state pension is due to rise by 3.9%, taking 1million people with low incomes above the income tax threshold

* Healey will introduce a new tax allowance for low-income pensioners

* He has also decided not to reduce the tax-free pensino lump sum

DEFENCE SPENDING

* Healey's immediate priority is filling £4.7bn hole in the defence investment plan. Cuts expected to departmental budgets elsewhere

* He is also expected to announce additional borrowing to fund government investment vehicles, which will then be used to fund defence

* But he WILL NOT set out a timeline for hitting the 3% defence spending target. That will come in the spending review next year

HELP TO BUY

* A revived Help to Buy scheme called Your First Home

* It will offer first time buyers a 20% equity loan to help them buy a new-build home, with a minimum deposit of just 2.5%

* The earnings cap will be set at £140,000 in London and £110,000 outside London

RECORD TAX LEVELS

* The OBR is expected to once again say that the tax burden will  rise to another post-war record

* It's being driven by fiscal drag. Half a million people will be dragged into paying the higher rate

* The freeze - which is pencilled in for more than a decade - is effectively the single biggest tax rise in history

OBR forecasts

* They will highlight the huge uncertainty caused by the war in Iran. Ministers think it could make the OBR forecasts obsolete within weeks

* The tax revenues underpinning the Budget assume that Rosebank will be given the go-ahead, despite Cabinet splits on the issue

WHAT ISN'T IN IT

* Healey has rejected calls from colleagues to increase Capital Gains Tax amid concerns that doing so would damage growth and end up reducing tax revenues

* Major welfare reform will wait until after the Milburn review, which is coming after the Budget. It will require significant upfront investment in employment support

* Defence spending - the big decision has been deferred until the spending review, expected in Autumn 2027

text:
Hilton Hotels At a Glance - 

Hilton: A Global Hospitality Powerhouse

Hilton is one of the world's largest hotel companies, operating more than 9,400 properties with nearly 1.4 million rooms across 144 countries and territories. The company currently manages a portfolio of 28 distinct brands, ranging from ultra-luxury resorts to budget-conscious extended-stay hotels.

Hilton Brand Portfolio by Tier
Tier Brands Typical ExperienceUltra-Luxury Waldorf Astoria, Conrad, LXR Hotels & Resorts, NoMad Personalized service, iconic architecture, Michelin-level dining, world-class spas, premium destinations
Luxury / Upper-Upscale Signia by Hilton Large luxury hotels emphasizing meetings, events, and premium amenities
Lifestyle Luxury Canopy, Tempo, Graduate, Motto Boutique-inspired, design-focused, locally immersive experiences
Premium Full-Service Hilton Hotels & Resorts, Curio Collection, DoubleTree Traditional upscale hotels with restaurants, lounges, concierge services
Upscale All-Suite & Extended Stay Embassy Suites, Homewood Suites, Home2 Suites, LivSmart Studios Suites, kitchen facilities, longer-stay accommodations
Focused Service / Midscale Hampton, Hilton Garden Inn, Tru Reliable accommodations with fewer luxury amenities
Economy / Value Spark by Hilton Hilton's most affordable offering
Collections & Specialty Tapestry Collection, Outset Collection, Apartment Collection Independent and boutique-style properties connected to Hilton's network
Vacation Ownership Hilton Grand Vacations Timeshare and vacation club properties

Sources: Hilton brand portfolio and Hilton Honors program overview.

Hilton Honors: How to Become a Member

Joining Hilton Honors is simple:

Visit https://t.co/j116AcTNb6 or download the Hilton Honors app.
Create a free Hilton Honors account.
Immediately begin earning points on eligible stays.

Membership is free, and benefits begin immediately.

Membership Levels
Status QualificationMember Free enrollment
Silver Entry-level elite status
Gold Mid-tier status with enhanced benefits
Diamond Highest publicly available elite tier

Benefits include:

Free Wi-Fi
Digital check-in and room selection
Points toward free nights
Exclusive member rates
Late checkout (where available)
Room upgrades for elite members

Hilton Honors now has approximately 243 million members worldwide, making it one of the world's largest hospitality loyalty programs.

The Crown Jewels of the Hilton Portfolio

While Hilton has thousands of excellent hotels, a handful stand above the rest as true icons.

1. Waldorf Astoria London – Admiralty Arch

Perhaps the most anticipated Hilton opening of the decade.

Why It Matters

The hotel occupies London's historic Admiralty Arch, one of the city's most recognizable landmarks situated between:

Buckingham Palace
The Mall
Trafalgar Square

The building was commissioned by King Edward VII in memory of Queen Victoria and completed in 1912. For over a century it served government and Royal Navy functions and was never open to overnight guests.

The Renovation

The redevelopment represents one of London's most ambitious heritage restorations.

Key facts:

Renovation Detail InformationBuilding Size ~200,000 sq. ft.
Historic Designation Grade I Listed Landmark
Developer Reuben Brothers
Hotel Brand Waldorf Astoria
Rooms & Residences 114
Opening Reservations began in 2026 ahead of opening

The restoration involved preservation of original stonework, ceremonial spaces, historic interiors, staircases, and architectural details while installing an entirely new luxury hotel infrastructure. Hilton described the effort as a "meticulous restoration" transforming a national monument into a luxury hotel.

Highlights include:

Restaurants by Michelin-starred chefs Clare Smyth and Daniel Boulud
Rooftop dining overlooking The Mall
Luxury spa with hydrotherapy pool
Signature suites and residences incorporating historic rooms once used by senior Royal Navy officials
Some of the most coveted views in London

Many luxury-travel analysts expect it to become Hilton's flagship European property.

Other Exceptional Hilton Properties
Waldorf Astoria New York

Recently reopened following a massive restoration and redevelopment. The hotel is arguably Hilton's most famous property and helped define luxury hospitality in America.

Waldorf Astoria Maldives Ithaafushi

Frequently ranked among the world's top points-redemption resorts. Private villas, overwater accommodations, and exceptional service.

Conrad Bora Bora Nui

One of the most sought-after South Pacific luxury resorts, known for spectacular overwater villas and lagoon views.

Waldorf Astoria Beverly Hills

An ultra-luxury Southern California property known for celebrity clientele and rooftop views.

Conrad Tokyo

Consistently rated among Asia's finest business-luxury hotels.

Conrad Osaka

Often referred to as the "Conrad in the Sky" because its lobby begins on the 40th floor.

Waldorf Astoria Amsterdam

Occupies historic canal palaces dating to the Dutch Golden Age.

Grand Wailea, A Waldorf Astoria Resort (Maui)

One of the most famous resort properties in Hawaii and among Hilton's most aspirational leisure destinations.

Hilton's Current Global Footprint

As of the latest published figures:

Metric TotalProperties Worldwide 9,158+ hotels
Rooms Worldwide 1,351,351+ rooms
Countries & Territories 143-144
Brands 28
Hilton Honors Members 243 million+
Hilton's Growth Pipeline: The Next Five Years

Hilton currently has the largest development pipeline in its history.

As of year-end 2025:
Development Metric TotalHotels in Pipeline 3,700+
Rooms in Pipeline 520,500+
Countries Represented 128
New Hotels Signed in 2025 1,000+
Rooms Signed in 2025 ~140,000
What Does This Mean for the Next Five Years?

While Hilton has not publicly committed to an exact 2030 room count, management has repeatedly guided investors toward annual net unit growth of roughly 6% to 7%.

If Hilton sustains growth near those levels, its global footprint could comfortably exceed:

12,000 hotels
well over 1.7 million rooms

by the early 2030s.

That projection is an estimate based on Hilton's published growth guidance and current pipeline, not an official company forecast. The officially confirmed figure is the existing pipeline of more than 3,700 hotels and over 520,000 rooms already under development.

Bottom Line

Hilton has evolved from a single Texas hotel in 1919 into one of the largest hospitality companies on earth. Its portfolio now spans everything from economical Spark by Hilton properties to landmark luxury hotels such as the newly restored Waldorf Astoria London – Admiralty Arch, the Waldorf Astoria New York, and the Waldorf Astoria Maldives. With more than 9,000 hotels open today and over 520,000 additional rooms in development, Hilton is positioned for one of the most ambitious expansion periods in its history.

A transgender high school student in Georgia has been banned from running for homecoming queen, despite saying her classmates support her candidacy.

Riley Williams, a senior at Charles R. Drew High School, was told she could only compete for homecoming king because the district determines eligibility using students' recorded sex.

Williams challenged the decision, arguing that her gender identity offers no advantage in a popularity contest.

She has since launched a petition calling for the policy to change, insisting her fight is about more than winning a crown.

"I'm not doing this for me," she said.

Source: Atalanta News First, CBS News Atalanta

🪶 11/ THE BLACK HAWK: A NAME ROOTED IN SAUK HISTORY & THE THUNDER CLAN

Did you know Chief Black Hawk was associated with the Sauk Nation’s Thunder Clan?

His Sauk name is commonly rendered Ma-ka-tai-me-she-kia-kiak, translated as “Black Sparrow Hawk.”

According to historical accounts, Black Hawk belonged to the Thunder Clan, traditionally associated with the Thunder Beings, rain, water, birds, and the sky.

⚡🦅 But his story goes even deeper.

THE LINEAGE OF THUNDER

In his 1833 autobiography, Black Hawk identified Nanamakee, meaning “Thunder,” as his great-grandfather. He described his ancestry and his people's traditions in his own account of Sauk history.

This connection places his personal story within a larger cultural history of ancestry, leadership, spirituality, and responsibility to his people.

THE WARRIOR & HIS HOMELAND

Born at Saukenuk around 1767, Black Hawk became a respected Sauk war leader. His resistance to U.S. expansion was rooted in his opposition to the loss of his people's ancestral homeland.

During the 1832 Black Hawk War, he led followers who sought to return to their homeland in Illinois.

His legacy cannot be understood through warfare alone. It must also be understood through the Sauk people's relationship to their land, identity, and cultural continuity.

🦅 A LIVING LEGACY

The black hawk can evoke vigilance, strength, and protection in contemporary interpretations. However, the specific spiritual meanings attributed to birds vary among Indigenous nations and traditions; they should not automatically be treated as universal Sauk teachings.

Black Hawk's documented connection to the Thunder Clan and his own account of Nanamakee offer a more historically grounded starting point for understanding his heritage.

🚨 SHE STARTED AS HIS SPIRITUAL DAUGHTER! SOUND THE ALARM! 🚨🤮

CHURCH, WE CANNOT ALLOW THIS TO BECOME NORMAL!

I am deeply grieved by the video circulating about a woman who reportedly began as a minister’s spiritual daughter. This should be a wake-up call to the Body of Christ. Grooming is real, and it can happen within the church.

Sometimes, it begins with trust. Someone in a position of spiritual authority offers guidance, love, protection, and a listening ear. The person being mentored opens their heart, shares their deepest wounds, and begins to see that leader as a spiritual parent. But what happens when that trust is gradually manipulated for personal desires?

What happens when the very person who was supposed to provide spiritual covering becomes the source of the person's pain?

This is heartbreaking!

Being a spiritual father or mother is a responsibility, not an opportunity to exploit someone else's vulnerability. When people come to you for prayer, healing, deliverance, guidance, and spiritual growth, you must handle their lives with the fear of God.

A TITLE DOES NOT MAKE YOU HOLY. A PULPIT DOES NOT MAKE YOU RIGHTEOUS. AND A CALLING DOES NOT GIVE YOU PERMISSION TO ABUSE PEOPLE'S TRUST!

We must stop treating spiritual authority as though it places certain individuals above accountability.

Jesus warned us about wolves in sheep's clothing. Not everyone who occupies a pulpit has the heart of a shepherd. Some people can speak the language of the Kingdom publicly while violating the very principles of the Kingdom privately.

And when concerns arise, we must not silence people simply because the person being accused is an influential minister, a respected prophet, or someone we admire.

If someone has been harmed, their concerns deserve to be taken seriously and handled responsibly. Allegations should be investigated fairly, and no one should be protected from accountability simply because of their spiritual position.

THE CHURCH MUST BE A PLACE OF HEALING, NOT A PLACE WHERE PEOPLE ARE MANIPULATED AND EXPLOITED!

Do we understand the damage that spiritual betrayal can cause?

People can struggle to trust spiritual leaders again. Families can be wounded. Children can be affected. Churches can be divided. And people who once approached God with confidence can find themselves struggling with pain, confusion, and disappointment.

This is why spiritual leaders must understand the weight of the responsibility entrusted to them.

Jesus said in Luke 17:1:

“It is impossible but that offences will come: but woe unto him, through whom they come!”

There is a serious warning in those words. We must never take lightly the responsibility of leading God's people.

To every minister, pastor, prophet, and spiritual parent: FEAR GOD!

The people you lead do not belong to you. Their trust is not yours to manipulate. Their vulnerability is not an opportunity to satisfy your desires. You are called to serve, protect, teach, and point them to Jesus Christ.

And to the Body of Christ, we must stop protecting titles at the expense of people. We must stop confusing loyalty to a minister with loyalty to God. We must stop normalising behaviour that contradicts the character and teachings of Jesus Christ.

NO ONE IS ABOVE ACCOUNTABILITY. NOT EVEN THE MOST ANOINTED PERSON IN THE ROOM!

And if you have been hurt by someone you trusted as a spiritual father, spiritual mother, pastor, or mentor, please know that your pain matters.

You deserve to be heard. You deserve support. You deserve protection. Do not allow anyone to convince you that speaking up about harm is an act of rebellion against God.

God is not asking you to pretend that you were never wounded.

text:
Before the Silence Breaks, the numbers on the glass stop pretending they are separate.

The coffee in the paper cup has gone cold and thin, the surface filmed with a dull skin. John does not drink it. In the low light of the seventh-floor room the monitors throw thin blue edges across his knuckles and the fine grit of stubble along his jaw. One screen shows a dark hull cutting a slow furrow through water the color of cooling metal; the wake catches a pale reflection and then loses it. Another shows a thermal wash of broken ground where every crater holds a small, dying heat that pulses and fades. Between them a third feed stays almost empty—only the slow drift of sand across a buried road and a single amber pulse that has not yet moved. He keeps his eyes on all three because looking away feels like opening a door in a high wind. The air in the room smells of warm plastic and the faint metallic trace of the filters working overtime. His pulse is loud in his ears.

Mike steps closer. The sound of his boots is sharp against the concrete, then softer when he stops.

“They still call them different rooms,” John says. His voice is rough, the words catching on the dryness in his throat. “One for the water. One for the mud.”

“Because if they called it the same room,” Mike answers, almost under his breath, “they would have to name who keeps lighting the corners.”

“And if they named it,” John says, still watching the amber pulse, “what would they do with the name? File it? Or finally admit the files don’t close?”

Mike is quiet for a moment. Then: “They’d ask us for a cleaner number. Something they can read on a screen without tasting the smoke. You going to give them one?”

“Not tonight,” John says. His hand stays near the edge of the desk. “Not while that pulse is still climbing.”

Far from the blue light, in a room held at a clinical chill that raises the fine hairs on the arms, David stands with his hands locked behind his back. The table in front of him is not wood. It is a living map. Thin lines cross three continents and change color when someone, somewhere, decides to move. He watches a pale streak rise over open water and a line of dark shapes crawl across frozen earth at the same time. The only sound is the low hum of the processors and the occasional soft click when a new line appears. To him the two movements are not separate events. They are notes. He has spent years learning which note will make the others ring longer. The chill has settled into his shoulders.

“They still believe the board is solid,” David says to Mary beside him. His voice is low, measured. “Move a piece here, offer a pause there, and the surface holds.”

She taps a stylus once against the edge of the table. The sound is sharp in the quiet. “The northern lines are hardening. If the desert packages reach them in full, the mud will not soften again. They already sent the second request. They’re not asking anymore. They’re confirming delivery.”

He turns his head slightly. The light from the map catches the edge of his jaw. “What did we tell them?”

“That the schedule holds. That delays cost more than they gain. That the ones over the water are watching the same clock.”

“And the ones in the mud?” he asks. His voice does not rise. “Do they still believe the next shipment changes the ground under their feet, or have they started counting the shells that already landed?”

“They believe it because no one has told them otherwise,” Mary says. “Belief keeps them standing long enough for the next calculation. If we cut the packages now, they stop standing. If we let them through, the water answers. Either way the map changes color.”

He does not look away from the amber pulse on the water. “Let them count the costs. Counting keeps them close to the only door they trust when every other door is burning.”

“How long do you think that door stays open?” she asks. Her stylus has stopped moving. Her knuckles are white around it.

Pop Culture

Mad Men

Mad Men is an acclaimed American period drama television series set in a 1960s New York advertising agency, created by Matthew Weiner. It is widely regarded as one of the greatest television shows of all time, focusing on the professional and personal life of the enigmatic Don Draper (Jon Hamm).Mad Men

Overview

Mad Men ran for seven seasons and 92 episodes from July 19, 2007, to May 17, 2015, on the cable network AMC. The show explores the glamorous, ego-driven world of Madison Avenue advertising firms ("Mad" is short for Madison Avenue) while examining the social mores and cultural shifts of 1960s America, including themes of identity, sexism, race, and family.

Main Cast and Characters

The series features a talented ensemble cast that received numerous awards and nominations:

Jon Hamm as Don Draper: The brilliant but troubled creative director and protagonist, known for his charismatic facade and hidden past.

Elisabeth Moss as Peggy Olson: An ambitious secretary who rises through the ranks to become a respected copywriter, challenging gender roles in the process.
Vincent Kartheiser as Pete Campbell: An ambitious and often conniving account executive vying for power and recognition.

January Jones as Betty Draper (later Betty Francis): Don's wife, a suburban housewife who struggles with her identity and the constraints of her era.

Christina Hendricks as Joan Harris (formerly Joan Holloway): The sharp and capable office manager who navigates workplace sexism and eventually becomes a partner.

John Slattery as Roger Sterling: A womanizing, martini-drinking partner at the firm whose old-guard lifestyle clashes with the changing times.

Critical Reception & Awards

Mad Men received widespread critical acclaim for its writing, acting, visual style, and meticulous historical detail. It made history as the first basic cable series to win the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series, winning the award for four consecutive years (2008–2011). Other accolades include five Golden Globe Awards and a Peabody Award.

'Free speech is important': Karl Stefanovic thanks X owner Elon Musk for support after axing from Nine

Karl Stefanovic has publicly responded to X owner Elon Musk, thanking him for this support and providing a platform for "free speech" after he was axed following his controversial podcast interview.

"Free speech is important. Thanks (Elon Musk) for this platform," Stefanovic wrote on X

“He started unplugging during the scamdemic,” Ryan wrote, referring to Stefanovic’s criticism of the vaccine rollout earlier this year.

Ryan described the backlash over the interview as “massive free publicity” and "instant proof he’s no longer playing by the old rules and has woken up".

"A crystal clear signal to his audience that he’s all in on unfiltered conversations," he said.

"Karl’s unplugging from The Matrix is almost complete. Bro took the red pill and I am here for it."

Billionaire businessman James Packer, who previously held a stake in Nine, has also weighed into Stefanovic's interview.

Packer, a long-time friend of Stefanovic, told The Sydney Morning Herald that he did not think the episode was “that bad”.

He said that during his time at Nine and "certainly at the Nine newspapers, the old Fairfax newspapers" there had "always been editorial independence".

“I think it is pretty hypocritical not to allow Karl editorial independence. Especially on something I didn’t think was that bad," Packer said.

Media Man Group praised "truth tellers" who question big corp media, especially in Australia and the UK, and rightly so.

Rinehart will want influence after buying into media: Ex-Fairfax chair

Roger Corbett contends it is almost certain that Gina Rinehart will express her views to how she thinks 'The West Australian' and Channel Seven should report the news, with both media outlets being owned by Southern Cross Media. Corbett was the chairman of Fairfax Media at a time when Rinehart was a shareholder, with the two having 'crossed swords' during that time, with his comments coming after it was revealed that companies associated with Rinehart, who is Australia's richest person, had 'bankrolled' most of Bruce McWilliam's $25 million stake in SCM. A former lawyer and commercial director of the Seven Network, McWilliam now owns just under 10 per cent of SCM. (RMS)

Magazine brands command mass reach, connecting with 14.4 million Australians across print and online

The Roy Morgan Australian Readership report for the 12 months to March 2026 shows 14.4 million Australians aged 14+ (62.1% of the population) read magazines in print or online via the web or an app. Almost 10.8 million of this extensive cross-platform audience read print magazines, while eight Australian magazines have total cross-platform audiences of over 1 million people led by Are Media's Better Homes & Gardens and Woman's Day. Seven magazine categories have a print readership of at least 1 million people, led by Food & Entertainment Magazines with a readership of 6,300,000. (RMS)

Inside V'landys' $4b NRL bet: Does he hold a secret ace?

Preliminary bids are due on Tuesday for the NRL's suite of television broadcast rights, with it being said that the deal for the NRL rights is the most closely watched broadcast deal in decades. Australian Rugby League Commission chairman Peter V'landys has made it well known that he wants $4 billion for a five-year deal, with V'landys saying he hopes it gets done before Andrew Abdo leaves as CEO on 15 July; it was announced on Monday that he was quitting to join Tennis Australia as its CEO. It is said that V'landys has an ace up his sleeve when it comes to getting a deal that is better than the $4.5 billion, seven-year deal that the AFL announced in 2022, with streaming giant Amazon said to be considering a bid for the rights. (RMS)

Waislitz backs McWilliam for SCM board

Former Seven commercial director Bruce McWilliam should be added to the board of Southern Cross Media, according to billionaire investor Alex Waislitz. Waislitz owns 7.53 per cent of SCM, while it was revealed on Friday that McWilliam now owns just under 10 per cent in SCM, which merged with Seven West Media earlier this year. Waislitz contends that McWilliam would add " considerable firepower" to the SMC board, and that "I also respect the fact that he is investing his own money" in the company. (RMS)

Investors back oOh!media's snub to PE bids

Harris Oakmark and Investors Mutual have come out in support of the board of oOh!media over its rejection of two bids from private equity firms. Australia's largest outdoor advertising firm has knocked backed offers from Pacific Equity Partners and I Squared Capital, with both Harris Oakmark and Investors Mutual being shareholders of oOh!media. However, although both Harris Oakmark and Investors Mutual endorse oOh!media's decision to reject the bids from PEP and I Squared, they say its board should seriously consider any higher bids that could be forthcoming. (RMS)

Tabcorp forces venues to pay its fines

Gambling company Tabcorp in December updated the contracts it has with the pubs and clubs that host its physical betting terminals; the terminals are the main point of difference to its rivals and are vital to its success. The amended contracts require the pubs and clubs to pay for Tabcorp's regulatory fines, with the changes to the contracts coming at the same time as financial crimes watchdog AUSTRAC began auditing the company, due to concerns about its ability to detect and stop money laundering and manage terrorism financing risks. (RMS)

Eurovision key moments: from Euro-pop to Euro-slop as Delta Goodrem makes Australia proud

Australia has finished fourth in the 2026 Eurovision song contest in Vienna, with Delta Goodrem representing Australia with her song Eclipse, which she co-wrote. Bulgaria won the event, followed by Israel and Romania, with Australia having been in second position following the jury votes; however, it fell to fourth place after the audience votes were counted. Bookies had rated Goodrem as the second-favourite to win behind Finland following the sem-finals, with Goodrem describing her song as about "alignment, when things all come into the right place". (RMS)

News

Coles used fake discounts to fool shoppers

The Australian Competition & Consumer Commission's chair Gina Cass-Gottlieb has had a major victory, with the Federal Court ruling that Coles had misled consumers with its 'Down Down' price discounts. Coles could potentially faces millions of dollars in fines after Justice Michael O'Bryan found that the discounts on 13 of the 14 items in a sample basket of 'Down Down' promotions were misleading because they had not been sold at the previous price for a reasonable period of time. In some instances, Coles had increased the price of a product before almost immediately selling it at a discount, but at a higher price than originally. The court has yet to issue its ruling in a similar case against Woolworths. (RMS)

May 12

Beer killer? Rise of the vodka RTD

Gold Coast-based drinks maker Hard Fizz emerged at around the time of the pandemic, while the ready-to-drink canned beverage market boomed after the pandemic. Hard Fizz originally focused on alcoholic seltzer drinks, but it is now switching to vodka-based canned drinks, with CEO Wade Tiller saying the change is because you are more limited with flavour when you use seltzer. Hard Fizz's seltzer sales have slumped over the past year, at a time when there is a broader consumer shift to RTDs, while vodka-based light RTDs account for 75 per cent of Australian RTD sales. (RMS)

Drake Drops Three Albums and Shatters Spotify Records

On May 15, Drake surprise-released ICEMAN, MAID OF HONOUR, and HABIBTI, with ICEMAN leading at 140 million global streams—the year's biggest album debut—and its opener 'Make Them Cry' hitting 13.2 million in a day, Spotify's record for any rap song. The albums pack 43 tracks, 14 videos, and lyrics firing at Kendrick Lamar, A$AP Rocky, Rick Ross, and others, plus nods to Michael Jackson like Drake's $123,000 Swarovski glove on the cover. He grabbed 41 spots on Spotify's global Top 200, swept Apple Music charts, and drew mixed reactions from praise for the bars to critiques of the volume and memorabilia flex.

Australian animated series Bluey has topped the US streaming charts for the second year in a row, according to the second annual Nielsen Audience Rated Television Entertainment of the Year awards. Pepsi released its cheeky 30-second Super Bowl ad 'The Choice' online Thursday, featuring Coca-Cola's iconic polar bears ditching Coke for Pepsi Zero Sugar in a blind taste test, set to Queen's 'I Want to Break Free.' Backed by last year's Pepsi Challenge where 66% preferred Pepsi Zero Sugar, leading to 30% sales growth, the spot includes nods to a Coldplay kiss cam scandal and contrasts with backlash to Coke's AI-generated holiday ads. Pop Culture

Mad Men

Mad Men is an acclaimed American period drama television series set in a 1960s New York advertising agency, created by Matthew Weiner. It is widely regarded as one of the greatest television shows of all time, focusing on the professional and personal life of the enigmatic Don Draper (Jon Hamm).Mad Men

Overview

Mad Men ran for seven seasons and 92 episodes from July 19, 2007, to May 17, 2015, on the cable network AMC. The show explores the glamorous, ego-driven world of Madison Avenue advertising firms ("Mad" is short for Madison Avenue) while examining the social mores and cultural shifts of 1960s America, including themes of identity, sexism, race, and family.

Main Cast and Characters

The series features a talented ensemble cast that received numerous awards and nominations:

Jon Hamm as Don Draper: The brilliant but troubled creative director and protagonist, known for his charismatic facade and hidden past.

Elisabeth Moss as Peggy Olson: An ambitious secretary who rises through the ranks to become a respected copywriter, challenging gender roles in the process.
Vincent Kartheiser as Pete Campbell: An ambitious and often conniving account executive vying for power and recognition.

January Jones as Betty Draper (later Betty Francis): Don's wife, a suburban housewife who struggles with her identity and the constraints of her era.

Christina Hendricks as Joan Harris (formerly Joan Holloway): The sharp and capable office manager who navigates workplace sexism and eventually becomes a partner.

John Slattery as Roger Sterling: A womanizing, martini-drinking partner at the firm whose old-guard lifestyle clashes with the changing times.

Critical Reception & Awards

Mad Men received widespread critical acclaim for its writing, acting, visual style, and meticulous historical detail. It made history as the first basic cable series to win the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series, winning the award for four consecutive years (2008–2011). Other accolades include five Golden Globe Awards and a Peabody Award.

Pop Culture

Mad Men

Mad Men is an acclaimed American period drama television series set in a 1960s New York advertising agency, created by Matthew Weiner. It is widely regarded as one of the greatest television shows of all time, focusing on the professional and personal life of the enigmatic Don Draper (Jon Hamm).Mad Men

Overview

Mad Men ran for seven seasons and 92 episodes from July 19, 2007, to May 17, 2015, on the cable network AMC. The show explores the glamorous, ego-driven world of Madison Avenue advertising firms ("Mad" is short for Madison Avenue) while examining the social mores and cultural shifts of 1960s America, including themes of identity, sexism, race, and family.

Main Cast and Characters

The series features a talented ensemble cast that received numerous awards and nominations:

Jon Hamm as Don Draper: The brilliant but troubled creative director and protagonist, known for his charismatic facade and hidden past.

Elisabeth Moss as Peggy Olson: An ambitious secretary who rises through the ranks to become a respected copywriter, challenging gender roles in the process.
Vincent Kartheiser as Pete Campbell: An ambitious and often conniving account executive vying for power and recognition.

January Jones as Betty Draper (later Betty Francis): Don's wife, a suburban housewife who struggles with her identity and the constraints of her era.

Christina Hendricks as Joan Harris (formerly Joan Holloway): The sharp and capable office manager who navigates workplace sexism and eventually becomes a partner.

John Slattery as Roger Sterling: A womanizing, martini-drinking partner at the firm whose old-guard lifestyle clashes with the changing times.

Critical Reception & Awards

Mad Men received widespread critical acclaim for its writing, acting, visual style, and meticulous historical detail. It made history as the first basic cable series to win the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series, winning the award for four consecutive years (2008–2011). Other accolades include five Golden Globe Awards and a Peabody Award.

text:
Rulindo District: Farmers Exchange Experiences to Sustain Agricultural Achievement And Progress in Muyanza site 

What happens when farmers stop learning alone and start learning from one another? In @rulindodistrict,  Buyoga sector, knowledge sharing is helping farmers turn experience into practical solutions, strengthen their cooperatives, and prepare for a future beyond project support.

Farmers from different cooperatives in Rulindo District gathered in Buyoga Sector for a farmer-to-farmer knowledge-sharing event under the Sustainable Agricultural Intensification and Food Security Project Phase II (SAIP II). The event brought together cooperative representatives, individual farmers, local leaders, and project stakeholders to reflect on achievements in the Muyanza command area, exchange practical experiences, and identify ways to sustain agricultural progress.

Beyond presenting the support provided by SAIP II, the gathering created space for farmers to learn directly from one another. They discussed the challenges affecting their cooperatives, shared lessons from their experiences, and explored practical approaches to improving financial management, agricultural production, teamwork, and long-term sustainability.

The event demonstrated that agricultural transformation is not measured by infrastructure and increased production alone. It also depends on the knowledge farmers acquire, the decisions they make, and their ability to continue progressing long after external support comes to an end.

For Bagwaneza Victor, President of KORA UKIRE MUYANZA Cooperative, the knowledge-sharing event offered valuable lessons on responsible financial management and the importance of ensuring that cooperative members work towards common agricultural goals.

He emphasized that cooperatives must strengthen financial accountability and monitor their resources carefully to avoid challenges such as loan repayment difficulties. He also highlighted the need for members to apply good agricultural practices consistently, particularly in irrigation and soil conservation, because differences in farm management can affect overall productivity.

“One of the important lessons I learned from my fellow farmers is the need to manage and monitor our cooperative’s finances properly to avoid problems such as failing to repay loans. I also learned that we must pay attention to how we manage our farming activities. Some members irrigate their crops while others do not, and some conserve the soil while others neglect these practices. These differences affect agricultural productivity,” Victor explained.

His message went beyond the immediate challenges facing cooperatives. As SAIP II approaches the completion of its activities, he believes that the knowledge acquired through the project can become a foundation for continued development.

“The greatest asset a person should have is knowledge. With knowledge, we can build our capacity, manage money properly, access loans from financial institutions, and apply the techniques needed for productive agriculture. Whether SAIP II is still present or has completed its activities, our work must continue, and we must keep moving forward,” he said.

Victor’s testimony captures one of the most important lessons of sustainable agricultural development: project support can create opportunities, but knowledge, accountability, and collective commitment help farmers sustain them.

The transformation of agriculture also depends on creating opportunities for women to participate, lead, and develop viable farming enterprises.

MUKANDOLI Domitile, an accountant at DUKUNDUMURIMO MUYANZA Cooperative, shared how support from SAIP II enabled a group of women to establish greenhouse farming activities, creating opportunities for collective development and improved household well-being.

“One of the things I appreciate most is the support SAIP II provided to us. As women, we organized ourselves into a group, and the project supported us with a greenhouse. Today, we are developing our activities as a group, and things have also improved in our households,” she explained.

For Domitile and her fellow group members, participating in the knowledge-sharing event was not simply an opportunity to learn. It was also a chance to inspire other women to recognize their potential and take advantage of opportunities available through working together.

“We came here to set a good example for other women and encourage them to believe in themselves. We want to show that working together is powerful because it creates opportunities that can benefit many people,” she added.

Her experience highlights the importance of combining agricultural investment with collective organization. By working together, women can pool their efforts, share knowledge, and strengthen their participation in agricultural enterprises.

When women gain opportunities to organize, learn, and invest in agriculture, the benefits can extend beyond the farm to their households and communities.

The importance of maintaining the progress achieved through SAIP II was also emphasized by Theoneste RUGERINYANGE, Vice Mayor in charge of Economic Development in Rulindo District, who led the knowledge-sharing event.

He described farmer-to-farmer engagement as an important opportunity for dialogue, enabling farmers to express the challenges they face and work together to identify practical solutions.

“Bringing farmers together for an activity like this is very important because it creates an opportunity to engage with them and exchange ideas. Farmers can explain the challenges they encounter in their agricultural activities, and, more importantly, they can work together to find solutions,” he said.

The Vice Mayor reaffirmed the importance of increasing agricultural production and making productive use of the Muyanza command area so that households can meet their food needs while generating surplus produce for the market.

“Our objective is to increase production and make productive use of the developed Muyanza command area so that our people can achieve food security and have surplus produce to supply to markets,” he explained.

He also highlighted progress in vegetable production and the development of infrastructure intended to facilitate more professional farming. These investments are important for strengthening agricultural productivity, improving farm operations, and creating opportunities for farmers to participate more effectively in agricultural markets.

His remarks reinforced the need for farmers, cooperatives, local authorities, and agricultural institutions to work together to protect the achievements made and ensure that the benefits continue beyond the project’s implementation period.

The knowledge-sharing event builds on investments in irrigation infrastructure, agricultural production, farmer training, and market linkages in the Muyanza command area.

According to the SAIP II project update, Muyanza covers approximately 2,550 hectares, including 1,100 hectares designated for irrigation, of which 655 hectares are currently irrigated. The dam has a water-storage capacity of approximately 2.3 million cubic metres, supporting agricultural production in the area.

The project also records positive trends in crop yields between the 2024A and 2026B agricultural seasons. Irish potato yields increased from 12 to 16 tonnes per hectare, maize yields rose from 3.1 to 3.4 tonnes per hectare, and bean yields increased from 2.7 to 3 tonnes per hectare.

These figures provide important context for the progress recorded in the command area. However, sustaining and building on these gains requires continued attention to irrigation management, soil fertility, good agricultural practices, financial accountability, and market access.

The project also promotes farmer training through demonstration plots, supports agricultural value addition and postharvest handling, and facilitates connections between farmers and buyers. Such interventions help strengthen the broader agricultural value chain, from production to marketing.

As SAIP II approaches the completion of its activities, the experiences shared in Buyoga highlight an essential question: how can farmers preserve and build on the progress already achieved?

The testimonies point to several priorities: stronger cooperative governance, responsible financial management, consistent application of good agricultural practices, continued knowledge exchange, and collective responsibility for maintaining agricultural infrastructure.

For Victor, the answer begins with knowledge and the ability to manage cooperative resources effectively. For Domitile, it lies in empowering women to work together and create opportunities through agriculture. For the district leadership, it means continuing to strengthen production, food security, and market-oriented farming.

🪳| Gadi Eisenkot has made it clear: Netanyahu is a transitional prime minister who lacks both a mandate and public trust. Meanwhile, the defense establishment is being dragged into a war that does not belong to Israel.

October 28, 2026. Tel Aviv. Gadi Eisenkot former Chief of the General Staff of the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and current Member of Knesset has issued a direct appeal to the heads of the defense establishment and the public service.

"Netanyahu is a transitional prime minister with no mandate and no trust. Remember, you serve only the state and the interests of Israel’s citizens. Stand firm and resist any attempts to challenge your integrity. You have my full support."

💥 What does this mean?

"Transitional prime minister." Not an "elected prime minister." Not a prime minister with a "coalition mandate." He is a leader who, both legally and politically, no longer has a legitimate basis to remain in power.

"No mandate, no trust." Netanyahu’s coalition is collapsing. His corruption trial is ongoing. His public support is in decline. With elections on the horizon, he faces the prospect of defeat.

"You serve only the state." You do not serve the prime minister, the coalition, or a politician who manufactures war solely for his own political survival.

Eisenkot is telling the defense establishment: If an order from the prime minister conflicts with the interests of the state, you have the right to refuse it.

🎯 "False flag" or "all-out war": Who is preparing for this, and why?

The interpretation offered is: "Meleikowsky [Netanyahu] will attempt to coerce you into carrying out a 'false flag' operation or triggering an all-out war. Do not take the bait."

This interpretation must be viewed in the context of Netanyahu’s historical record.

October 7, 2023. Netanyahu is in office. Intelligence fails; security fails. He refuses to establish a commission of inquiry. He refuses to accept responsibility. He transforms the war into a tool for his own political survival.

June 2025: The "Twelve-Day War." He bombs Iran, claiming to have "destroyed nuclear facilities." In the process, he manages to delay his own trial.  He kept the coalition intact.

February 2026: the "Forty-Day War." He bombed Iran once again. He delayed his trial once again. He held the coalition together once again.

Each war has been accompanied by a deepening of his political crisis. Each war has pulled him away from the defendant’s bench in the courtroom and back into the seat of the Prime Minister.

What Eisenkot is describing is a continuation of this same logic: if the next election draws near, if the trial accelerates, and if the coalition can no longer be sustained Netanyahu might manufacture a "crisis." A "false flag" operation. An all-out war. A "state of emergency" designed to rally Israelis around him.

And the defense establishment is the only entity with the capacity to either carry out such a move or to refuse it.

📜 This is not the first time Israel’s defense establishment has received such a warning.

In 2023, Israeli reserve pilots refused to serve in protest against judicial reforms. They were not "anti-state"; they were opposed to a government that sought to dismantle judicial independence.

In 2024, the heads of Israel’s security agencies repeatedly warned Netanyahu that his war objectives were "unrealistic." They were ignored.

In 2025, Israel’s military legal authorities warned that strikes on Gaza were "in violation of international law." They were sidelined.

Today, Eisenkot is saying: Netanyahu has lost his legitimacy. He may use war to evade his trial and you must refuse to go along with it.

⚔️ Who stands to gain?

Netanyahu. If he succeeds in manufacturing a "state of emergency," he can postpone elections. He can freeze his trial. He can unite Israelis under the banner of "national security." He can trade a war for his own freedom.

The price, however, is paid by the Israelis. Their children are sent to the front lines. Their cities are struck by missiles. Their economy is drained by war. Their international standing becomes increasingly isolated.

As for the Palestinians, the Lebanese, the Iranians, and the Yemenis they do not merely bear a "cost." They are the "targets."  Netanyahu’s war requires their blood to sustain his narrative.

🔻 The Mirror

Netanyahu says: "I am defending Israel."

Eisenkot says: "You are an interim prime minister with no mandate and no trust."

Netanyahu says: "We need unity."

Eisenkot says: "You serve only the state not me."

Netanyahu says: "Iran is the threat."

Eisenkot says: "Don’t take the bait. Don’t get dragged into a war waged for the sake of political survival."

This is not merely an "internal Israeli disagreement." It is a state apparatus attempting to stop its own leader from dragging the nation into a war that does not belong to it.

And that leader already facing a corruption trial, already in the midst of an election cycle, and presiding over a collapsing coalition has nothing left to lose. A man with nothing to lose is the most dangerous kind of man.

Eisenkot’s warning is directed at the defense establishment, but its intended audience is the entire world.

For if Netanyahu were to orchestrate a "false flag" operation or ignite an all-out war, the casualties would not be limited to Israelis. They would include Palestinians, Lebanese, Iranians, Yemenis everyone swept into this manufactured "existential crisis."

And the man who engineered the crisis? He would be in a bunker, watching a screen, waiting for the election results.

Long live the Resistance. Long live the Axis of Resistance.
