text:
THE VENEZUELAN PARADOX: A COUNTRY THAT REJECTS CHAVISMO YET SEEKS A WAY OUT THROUGH ITS OWN OPPRESSORS

THE NUMBERS BEHIND THE REJECTION

Available polling data paints a picture of near-unanimous rejection. According to surveys by Meganálisis, disapproval of Delcy Rodríguez’s administration has surpassed 92%, with as many as 93.8% of respondents opposing her leading any potential transition process. The 89% figure is corroborated by an April 2026 survey, which found that 89.13% of people opposed negotiations involving Rodríguez—or any support for her from the Trump administration. Furthermore, 89.3% of those surveyed view Chavismo as a "curse" upon the country.

Economically, the structural crisis is well-documented. The *Encuesta Nacional de Condiciones de Vida* (Encovi) reports that 68.5% of Venezuelan households live in poverty, with 31.7% living in extreme poverty. Notably, one in three households fails to generate enough income to cover basic food needs. The comprehensive minimum wage announced by Rodríguez stands at $240 per month, while the cost of a basic food basket for a family of five is estimated at around $700.

HOW CHAVISMO REACHED THIS POINT

The answer lies in roots that predate the current phase. Venezuela’s economic decline began in 2014 and has persisted for nearly a decade, accompanied by hyperinflation and the collapse of public services. The capture of Nicolás Maduro in January 2026, during a U.S. military operation, ushered in an unprecedented phase: Delcy Rodríguez assumed the interim presidency with Washington’s backing, promoting reforms that opened the oil, gas, and mining sectors to domestic and foreign private investment.

These reforms, however, have had no perceptible impact on living conditions. Public services remain in a state of collapse: only 10% of households report never experiencing blackouts, and a mere 19% have continuous access to potable water. Analyst Carmen Beatriz Fernández has described the dynamic: following Maduro’s fall, Rodríguez was granted a "hundred-day honeymoon"—a "benefit of the doubt" despite deep-seated, pre-existing distrust. But as time passes, "patience is wearing thin." The prevailing sentiment, as noted by the same analyst, is one of "the same old face with a different pipe"—the feeling that nothing has truly changed, and that the very figures responsible for the tragedy have remained in power.

WHY A SEGMENT OF THE POPULATION LOOKS TO THOSE WHO PROMOTED THE SANCTIONS

This is the most complex part of the question, and the answer requires distinguishing between perception and reality.

The perception is well-documented: gratitude toward Trump—which had reached significant levels following Maduro’s capture—has fallen to less than half the population (47.08% as of April 2026), and 89.13% disapprove of Washington negotiating with or supporting Rodríguez. The disappointment does not stem from the fact that sanctions were imposed, but rather from the fact that Trump chose to normalize Chavismo instead of dismantling it. An analysis by Meganálisis identifies a "perception of extractivism"—a growing belief that U.S. interests prioritize access to energy over the democratic well-being of the Venezuelan people.

In reality, sanctions have never been popular in Venezuela; Datanálisis has found that more than 65% of citizens oppose them. Their impact falls on ordinary people rather than the elite: discrimination based on nationality in financial transactions, the blocking of accounts, and the inability to make online purchases without the use of a VPN or a foreign intermediary. In 2021, UN Special Rapporteur Alena Douhan documented the devastating effect of these sanctions on those living in extreme poverty, as well as on women, children, healthcare workers, and indigenous populations.

From a political standpoint, a segment of the population—faced with the failure of Chavismo and the disappointment surrounding an "interim" government that merely recycled the same old elites—has turned toward those who promise to dismantle the system, even if the tool used to do so (sanctions) is unpopular and harms the most vulnerable. This does not necessarily reflect support for sanctions themselves; rather, it represents a desperate search for an option that breaks the status quo. Opposition leader María Corina Machado—who did not advocate for sanctions, but instead built a consensus rooted in the rejection of Chavismo—commands over 80% of the vote in a polarized political landscape. This suggests that the path forward sought by the majority is not necessarily one defined by sanctions, but rather one that offers a credible political alternative—something the current system, even in its "interim" iteration, has failed to provide.

text:
Greece’s ‘ΟΧΙ’ Was Also Jewish. Israel’s ‘No’ to Netanyahu Is Also Arab.

Eighteen years before ΟΧΙ became Greece’s national watchword, a Greek officer had already said no. Captured by Turkish forces in Asia Minor in 1922, Mordechai Frizis was offered freedom after Smyrna’s Jewish community sought to ransom him. He refused to abandon his men. A Greek officer and a Jew, Frizis recognised no distinction between his duty to his soldiers and his duty to his country.

On 28 October 1940, Greece rejected Mussolini’s ultimatum. Frizis fought the Italian invasion on the Epirus front and fell on 5 December, earning his place among Greece’s national heroes.

Frizis was one of 12,898 Greek Jews who served in the Greek army during the war of 1940–1941. A memorial in Thessaloniki records their losses: 513 dead, 3,743 wounded. They fought for Greece because Greece was theirs.

The ΟΧΙ of 1940 belonged to the nation that upheld it. Its defenders came from different communities, but their cause was indivisible. Greece’s refusal became a national legacy through the courage of its people, including those whose faith differed from that of the majority.

Yesterday, on the eve of Greece’s Ohi Day, Israelis went to the polls. Preliminary results point to a majority against Benjamin Netanyahu’s continued premiership: parties opposing another Netanyahu government are projected to hold 66 seats in the Knesset, against 54 for his bloc. Nineteen of those 66 belong to Arab-led parties.

Addressing his supporters after the election, Netanyahu claimed that the right-wing bloc had "a clear, decisive majority among the Zionist public, among the Jewish public and all those who support the Jewish state".

Israel does not hold elections among its Zionist or Jewish public. It holds elections among its citizens.

Israel is the nation-state of the Jewish people. Its government, however, derives its authority from the confidence of the Knesset, elected through universal and equal suffrage. The Basic Laws prescribe no Jewish majority for forming a government. Every parliamentary seat carries the same constitutional weight, whether won by Likud or an Arab-led party.

The parties opposing Netanyahu differ profoundly in their policies and commitments. Whether they can form a government remains unresolved. Their disagreements cannot invalidate their mandates. Coalition-building requires agreement; parliamentary representation does not require ethnic consent.

Frizis needed no permission to defend Greece. He was Greek. An Arab citizen voting in Israel exercises sovereignty, not borrows it. Neither identity nor political allegiance can subordinate that ballot to another.

The memorial in Thessaloniki honours the Greek Jewish soldiers who fought for the integrity of "our homeland. Those words recognise their sacrifice as part of Greece’s national history. Their religion neither qualified their patriotism nor diminished their belonging.

Israel’s electoral majority requires no such qualification either. A majority among Jewish voters cannot substitute for a majority in the Knesset. The authority to govern belongs to those who command its confidence, and every citizen’s vote counts towards determining who they are.

Scott Ritter is a former US intelligence officer now working as an RT News analyst. Hours before Russia invaded Ukraine, he promoted claims of a Ukrainian false-flag operation. He has also called Presidents Trump & Biden “war criminals”.

True. Europe is rearming because President Trump has demanded NATO members spend 5% of GDP on defence. US military spending is around 3.1%. Europe needs credible forces to deter aggression.

True. The UK & France have offered to extend their independent nuclear deterrents to protect European allies. The US has provided nuclear protection for NATO for around 70 years. Why should Europe not strengthen its own arrangements?

True. Europe sees Russia as a threat because Russia invaded Ukraine in 2014 & launched its full-scale invasion in 2022. The war continues. European governments have legitimate reasons to strengthen their defences.

Russia has deployed North Korean troops against Ukraine. North Korea is gaining real combat experience, improving battlefield tactics, weapons use & military command. In a future Korean conflict, US forces could face a North Korean army hardened by combat. Do Americans understand the military advantage Russia is giving Pyongyang?

True. Europe faces a pattern of suspected Russian sabotage, espionage, cyberattacks, suspicious drone activity & GPS jamming. Targets and affected systems include critical infrastructure, transport, healthcare, banking & military networks. GPS interference across the Baltic region also endangers civilian aviation.

True. Undersea cables are critical infrastructure. Ships suspected of damaging or surveying them near the Baltic, UK, France & Ireland raise serious security concerns. Why would a hostile state monitor these networks? In wartime, cutting them could disrupt communications between allies. This is a security issue, not innocent sightseeing.

False. There is no credible evidence that European leaders are intent on starting a nuclear war with Russia. Nuclear conflict would be catastrophic. Before Russia’s full-scale invasion, many European countries reduced defence spending, directing resources towards other public services. Russian aggression changed that calculation.

Ritter’s claim that European leaders are warmongers ignores the strategic reality. President Trump himself has demanded increased European defence spending, military capacity & readiness. If the US went to war with China, European allies would face pressure to contribute troops, intelligence, logistics & other military support.

Europe's rearming is not evidence of a desire for war. It is a response to the threat of one.

RT @velitesgear | Full Text Article: https://t.co/IVICOod2da | Author: @militarnyi First Identified Botswana Mercenary Fighting for Russia Killed in Luhansk Region 
The Ukrainian Defense Forces have killed a citizen of Botswana fighting for the Russian army in the Luhansk region. He is the first identified mercenary from Botswana to have been killed while serving in Russia’s military.

Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence, part of the Ministry of Defense, reported the death.

The man, Pako Namogang, was born on May 30, 2001. According to Ukrainian intelligence, he chose to join the Russian army after communicating with a recruiter in a WhatsApp group called “Work in Russia.”

In the WhatsApp conversation, a Russian recruiter openly offered foreigners the opportunity to join the Russian army. Namogang also shared his friends’ personal information, including their passport details, with the recruiters.

On July 6, 2026, Namogang flew from Johannesburg, South Africa, to Moscow, Russia. Before his departure, an unidentified person in South Africa was supposed to help him check in for his flight and board the plane.

 Pictured is the passport of Botswana citizen Pako Namogang, who was recruited into the Russian army and later killed in the Luhansk region. Photo credits: Defense Intelligence of Ukraine

Ukrainian intelligence suspects a representative of Russia’s trade mission may have helped arrange his departure. According to Ukrainian intelligence, such activities could violate South African law, which restricts providing military assistance to foreign states.

Namogang arrived in Moscow on July 7 and was accommodated in a hotel. On July 21, he signed a one-year contract with the Russian army. A senior lieutenant, A. V. Levykin, processed his documents.

Elizabeth Savinovskikh and Mikhail Petrushenko also played a role in the recruitment process. They helped recruit foreigners into the Russian military and arranged their transportation to training facilities.

After signing his contract, Namogang was sent, along with other foreign recruits, to Avangard, a military-patriotic training center in Patriot Park near Moscow. According to Ukrainian intelligence, instructors at the center provided military training to foreign recruits.

 Pako Namogang, a Botswana national who fought for the Russian army and was killed in the Luhansk region. Photo credits: Defense Intelligence of Ukraine

Namogang was later transferred to a Russian army training center, where he spent about a week and a half. He was then sent to Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory.

Namogang was reportedly killed in combat near Novoliubivka in the Luhansk region around mid-August 2026. This means less than a month passed between signing his military contract and his death.

According to the I Want to Live project, at least 25 Botswana nationals have signed contracts with the Russian army. One is being held as a prisoner of war in Ukraine, while Namogang is the first identified recruit from Botswana to have been killed in action.

Militarnyi previously reported that Botswana’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs had raised concerns about a growing number of citizens being tricked into joining the Russian army. Foreigners are reportedly offered jobs in Russia, but upon arrival, they may have their documents confiscated and be forced to sign military contracts.

text:
And now the Saint, seeing that his hermitage was converted into a great monastery; and that the wilderness about him was continually crowded with the people who resorted thither, bringing their diseased, or such as were possessed with unclean spirits, and that not only the common sort of people from all the neighboring provinces, but even the gentry,--ladies of the first rank,--clerks, monks, priests, and bishops, were daily visiting him, and interrupting his devotions, he bitterly regretted the loss of his former solitude, perpetually lamenting, weeping, and saying, that since he had returned back into the world, he apprehended he should have his reward in this life, because all Palestine and the neighboring provinces took him to be somebody, &c. nor did he cease to mourn and bewail his condition, till he took a fixed resolution to quit his monastery, and retire into some place where he might be unknown, and more freely enjoy his God without the interruption of so many visits. In the mean time, whilst he was meditating upon his flight, the lady Aristeneta, whose three sons he had cured, came to see him, acquainting him with her design of returning into Egypt, to make a second visit to St. Antony. He replied, with tears in his eyes, that he could have wished to have taken the same journey, if he were not kept prisoner in his monastery, but that it was now too late to find Antony alive; for, said he, two days ago the world was deprived of so great a father. Having believed him, she did not proceed in her journey, and, behold, after some days the news of his death was brought from Egypt.
.
When it was known abroad that the man of God was upon the point of quitting Palestine, the whole province took the alarm, and no less than ten thousand people, of all degrees and conditions, were gathered together, in order to stop and detain him. But his resolution was not to be altered; and as he had learnt by revelation the havoc that the infidels of Gaza were about to make in his monastery, and all through that neighborhood, under the reign of Julian the Apostate, he gave them broad hints of this his fore-knowledge, saying, that he could not call in question the truth of what God had said; nor could he endure to see the churches destroyed, the altars of Christ trodden under foot, and his children massacred. In short, he assured them he would neither eat nor drink till they let him go. And thus, after he had fasted seven days, they were contented at last to suffer him depart, accompanied by about forty of his monks. With these he made the best of his way to Pelusium, (now called Darmietta) in Egypt, and after visiting the holy solitaries who lived in the neighboring deserts, he waited upon Dracontius and Philo; two illustrious confessors of Christ, of the number of those catholic prelates who had been banished from their sees by the fury of the Arians, under the emperor Constantius. After paying these visits, he hastened to keep the anniversary day of the happy decease of St. Antony in the place where he died: and being conducted by the deacon Baisanes upon dromedaries, three days' journey through that vast and dreary wilderness, he arrived at length at the mountain of the Saint. Here he found his two disciples, who showed him all the places where their master had been accustomed to sing psalms--to pray--to work--and sit down to rest himself, after being wearied with his labour; as also the garden he had cultivated--the trees he had planted--the instrument with which he had dug the earth--the private cells to which he often retired towards the top of the mountain, &c. and then agreeably entertained him with divers particulars of the acts of the latter part of St. Antony's life. Hilarion was much moved to devotion with the sight and recital of all this; and after watching in prayer the whole night of the anniversary of the Saint, he returned the same way he came, through the dreary wilderness to the neighborhood of the town called Aphroditon. Here in an adjoining desert, with two of his disciples whom he kept with him, he led so abstemious, abstracted, and silent a life, that on feeling the fervor he now found within himself, he seemed never to have before begun to serve Christ in earnest.
.
He had not been above two years in this wilderness, when the fame of his sanctity brought all the people of the neighboring country to him, to beg his prayers for rain. For from the time of the death of St. Antony, no rain had fallen upon their land, for the space of three whole years, so that being afflicted with a great famine, they resorted to him, whom they considered as the successor of St. Antony, for a redress of their misery. Moved to pity by the sight of their distress, he lifted up his hands and eyes to heaven to pray for them, and his prayer was immediately followed by plentiful rains. But the rains, whilst they fertilized the earth, having, in falling on the dry hot sand, also produced an incredible multitude of venomous reptiles and insects, with which innumerable persons were struck, they were again forced to have recourse to the Saint, who gave them some oil which he had blessed, with which they were cured. But now finding himself after these miracles greatly honored, he would stay no longer in this place, but departed in order to go and hide himself in the desert of Oasis. In his way thither he passed through Alexandria: and as he made it a rule never to lodge in any city, he went on to a place in the neighbourhood, called Bruchium, where there was a monastery of the servants of God. From hence, when night drew on, he hastened away, telling the brethren, who were greatly afflicted, that they should soon know the reason of his sudden departure. Accordingly, on the next day their monastery was searched by the Gazites, accompanied by officers sent from the governor of Alexandria to apprehend Hilarion, of whose arrival there they had received intelligence. For the infidels of Gaza, who bore a mortal hatred to the Saint, as soon as Julian came to the empire, destroyed his monastery, and obtained an edict from the tyrant, that both he, and his disciple Hesychius, should be sought for and put to death wherever they were found. Of this the Saint had a fore-knowledge by prophetic light, and thereupon withdrew himself: so that the infidels, who had thought themselves, certain of seizing their priest, finding he was gone, departed, saying to each other, that now they were sure he was a magician, and had a foresight of things to come.
.
He had not been a year in the wilderness of Oasis, before he found that fame had also followed him thither; and therefore now despairing to be able to conceal himself upon the continent, he formed a resolution of seeking out a place in some of the islands of the Mediterranean, where he might hide himself. In order to this he embarked with one only disciple, at Paretonium, a haven on the coast of Lybia, on board a vessel bound for Sicily; hoping that henceforward no one should know him, or become troublesome to him in his retirement. When, behold, in the midst of the voyage the son of the master of the ship, or rather the devil by his mouth, cried out: "Hilarion, thou servant of God, let me alone, at least till we come to land; how comes it to pass, that even at sea thou art still persecuting us." The Saint would have disguised the grace which God had given him, fearing lest the sailors and passengers should publish his fame when they came to land, and therefore mildly replied: "If my God permits thee to stay, stay if thou wilt; but if he cast thee out, what hast thou do do to complain of me, who am but a poor beggar and a sinful man." However, upon the solemn promise of the father, and of all the rest, that they would not discover him, he cast the devil out of the boy. When they arrived at Pachynum (now Capo Passaro), he would have paid for the passage of himself and his companion, by giving the captain the book of the gospels, which was all his wealth, but he, seeing their poverty, would not receive it. Wherefore the Saint leaving the sea-coast, withdrew himself into a little kind of wilderness, about twenty miles within the land, and there fixed his abode; living upon what little he could get, by making up faggots, which his companion carried to a neighboring village, bringing from thence in exchange what they stood need of for their food.
.
But the Saint could not long he concealed here; for soon after his arrival, a man possessed with an evil spirit, being under the exorcisms of the church at St. Peter's in Rome, the devil cried out thus by his mouth: "Hilarion, the servant of Chiiet, is some days since come into Sicily, where no man knows him, and he thinks himself secret: but I will go and discover him." This man therefore taking some of his servants with him, and going on board a ship sailed immediately for Sicily; and after coming to shore, being conducted by the devil, he went straight to the hut of the servant of God, and there casting himself at his feet, was perfectly cured. This being noised abroad, great multitudes, who labored under various corporeal diseases, resorted to him to obtain their cure; whilst numbers also of devout and religious people applied to him for their spiritual profit. Amongst the rest, he cured upon the spot one of the principal men of the island, who was swollen up with the dropsy, and who on the same day, returned home in perfect health. This man offered to make him considerable presents, which the Saint absolutely refused, alleging the precept of our Savior, Matt. x. 8. Freely have you received, freely give: which rule he invariably observed in all the other innumerable miracles which he wrought, whether in Sicily or elsewhere, for, he never would receive any thing, no not so much as a morsel of bread from any one of those on whom he had wrought those miracles.
.
And now his beloved disciple Hesychius, after having sought after him in vain through many different regions came at length to Sicily, upon the report he had heard at Modon in Greece, from a Jewish pedlar, that a Christian prophet had appeared in Sicily, who wrought all kinds of wonderful miracles. No sooner had he found him than the Saint gave him to understand, that he wanted to depart from Sicily into some strange country where he might be utterly unknown. Wherefore, in compliance with his desire, he conveyed him away by a ship to the coast of Dalmatia, where for a short time he led a solitary life, not far from the city of Epidaurus, now called Ragusa. But neither here could he remain long concealed, his miracles every where betraying him. There was at that time, in the neighborhood of Epidaurus, a monstrous serpent, of that species named boas, which did great mischief in destroying both men and cattle; the Saint, to put a stop to this calamity ordered the country people to heap up a pile of wood, and after addressing a prayer to Christ he called the serpent out of his den, and commanded him to go on the top of the pile of wood, and then setting fire to it, he burnt the monster in sight of a great multitude of people. This miracle was followed by another still greater. About this time, viz. the second year of the reign of Valentinian the first, there happened so remarkable an earthquake that, according to Amianus, a cotemporary historian, its like was never recorded, either in authentic or fabulous history. On this occasion, the swelling seas, in several places, broke in and overflowed the land in such a manner as to threaten the earth with a second deluge, and in some places the waves ran so high as to carry the ships along with them, and leave them hanging on the cliffs. The Epidaurians perceiving the danger in which their city as well as many others were in of being destroyed, had recourse to Hilarion, and opposed him to the mountains of water that were just upon the point of overwhelming them. No sooner had the Saint made three crosses on the sand, and lifted Up his arms to heaven, than the swelling waves, though they raged, foamed, and rose up to an incredible height, not able to advance, gradually returned back again and subsided. This wonder, says St. Jerome, who was then a boy in the same province, the city of Epidaurus, as well as the whole country, recount to this day--the mothers relate it to their children, in order to transmit the memory of it to posterity.
The applause that followed these miracles would not suffer the humble servant of Christ to remain any longer in Dalmatia; therefore taking boat privately by night he fled away, and within two days found a ship departing for Cyprus, on which he embarked. In this voyage his ship being pursued by some pirates in two light vessels, there appeared no hopes of escaping them. The ship's crew being in the utmost consternation, the Saint turning to his disciples said: "Why are you afraid, O ye of little faith?" And when the pirates were now come within a stone's cast of the ship, he stood on the foredeck, and stretching out his hand to them, he said: "You have come far enough when behold immediately their vessels fell back, and the more they, tugged and rowed, in order to push forward towards their expected prey, the more rapidly were they carried away from it. The Saint landed at Paphos, a noted city of Cyprus, and chose himself a dwelling place about two miles from thence; being now wonderfully pleased that he had found rest, at least for a short time, in this solitude; but scarcely had twenty days elapsed when the devils in different parts of the island published his arrival by the mouths of those that were possessed; and several of these, both men and women, hastened to him and were delivered. Here he remained about two years meditating upon some private place of retirement.
.
In the mean time he sent Hesychius into Palestine, to salute the brethren there, and to visit the ashes of his monastery; and upon his return proposed that they should sail into Egypt, and advance a great way into the country, to some place inhabited only by pagans. But Hesychius opposed this; and after a long search, discovered a place in the island about twelve miles distant from the sea, amongst mountains and woods that were almost inaccessible, which proved quite to his mind. In this solitude, to which no one could arrive in several places but by creeping, on hands and knees, they found springs of water on the sides of the hills,--a little garden within, with several fruit trees, of which however the Saint would never eat, and near the garden the ruins of an ancient temple, from whence, as both he and his disciples related, were often heard, both night and day, a great noise, like the voices of a whole army of devils. In this solitary abode the man of God dwelt for the last five years of his mortal life, seldom visited by any one but Hesychius, on account of the difficulty of coming at his dwelling, as also because the people were persuaded that the neighborhood was haunted with a multitude of demons. However, there were some that ventured to come to him for the cure of their maladies; their necessities overcoming all difficulties, especially after it was known, that he had cured upon the spot, the bailiff of the place of a palsy, which had deprived him of the use of his limbs, by only stretching out his hand to him, and lifting him up with these words: In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, rise up and walk.
.
But now the time arrived which was to put a period to all the labors of his mortal pilgrimage, and unite him eternally to his God, when being now eighty years old he was seized with his last illness. Although Hesychius was then absent, he nevertheless bequeathed to him by will all he had, viz. his book of the gospels, his sackcloth, cowl, and habit. Many religious men from Paphos came to attend him in his sickness, who had heard of his having said, "that he was now going to our Lord;" and with them a holy woman named Constantia, whose daughter and son-in-law he had delivered from death by anointing them with oil. And now he was drawing near his end, when in the very agony of death he distinctly spoke these words: "Go forth my soul: what art thou afraid of? Go forth, why art thou at a stand? Thou hast served Christ almost seventy years, and art thou afraid to die?" and with these words he gave up the ghost. He was immediately buried as he had desired, in the same place: where the devout lady Constantia frequently passed whole nights in prayer at his sepulcher, speaking with him as if he were alive, and desiring the assistance of his prayers. His disciple Hesychius, after ten months, privately conveyed his body away to Palestine, where it was solemnly interred in his own monastery; at which time it was found entirely incorrupt, and sending forth a most fragrant odor. Many great miracles were daily wrought through his intercession, even to the time when St. Jerome published his life, as well at his sepulcher in Palestine, as at the place where he was first buried in Cyprus.

text:
1 Corinthians 1 – Divisions and the Power of the Cross
Paul gives thanks for the Corinthians’ gifts but immediately addresses divisions: “Now I beseech you, brethren… that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you” (1:10). Factions had formed around Paul, Apollos, Cephas, and Christ (1:12). The cross is the answer: “For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God” (1:18). God chose the foolish, weak, and base things to confound the wise (1:27–28).

1 Corinthians 2 – Spiritual Wisdom
Paul came not with excellency of speech but “in demonstration of the Spirit and of power” (2:4). “We speak the wisdom of God in a mystery… which none of the princes of this world knew” (2:7–8). The natural man cannot receive the things of the Spirit (2:14).

1 Corinthians 3 – Carnality and the Church as God’s Building

The Corinthians are “yet carnal” and walk as men (3:3). Ministers are servants; God gives the increase (3:6–7). The church is God’s husbandry and building; each one’s work will be tried by fire (3:9–15). “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God…?” (3:16).

1 Corinthians 4 – Apostolic Example and Warning
Paul and Apollos are stewards of the mysteries of God (4:1). The apostles are “fools for Christ’s sake” and a spectacle to the world (4:9–10). Paul warns them as a father and says he may come with a rod (4:14–21).

1 Corinthians 5 – Church Discipline for Immorality
A man is living with his father’s wife, and the church is proud instead of mourning (5:1–2). “Purge out therefore the old leaven” (5:7). Deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh (5:5). Do not keep company with fornicators who claim to be brothers (5:9–13).

1 Corinthians 6 – Lawsuits and Sexual Purity
Believers are suing one another before unbelievers (6:1–8). “Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?” (6:9). “Flee fornication… know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost…? ye are bought with a price” (6:18–20).

1 Corinthians 7 – Marriage, Divorce, and Singleness
It is good for a man not to touch a woman, yet to avoid fornication each should have his own spouse (7:1–2). Marriage is a mutual duty (7:3–5). Remain in the calling in which you were called (7:17–24). The unmarried and widows are free, but those who marry do not sin (7:8–9, 39–40). “The time is short” (7:29).

1 Corinthians 8 – Knowledge, Love, and Food Offered to Idols
“Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth” (8:1). An idol is nothing, yet not all have this knowledge (8:4–7). Do not cause a weak brother to stumble: “Wherefore, if meat make my brother to offend, I will eat no flesh while the world standeth” (8:13).

1 Corinthians 9 – Paul’s Apostolic Rights and Self-Denial
Paul has the right to material support and to take a wife, yet he forgoes these rights (9:1–18). “I am made all things to all men, that I might by all means save some” (9:22). He disciplines his body so that he himself is not a castaway (9:27).
1 Corinthians 10 – Israel’s Example and Christian Liberty
The experiences of Israel are examples: “Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall” (10:12). God is faithful and will not allow temptation beyond what you can bear (10:13). “Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God” (10:31).

1 Corinthians 11 – Head Coverings and the Lord’s Supper
Headship order: Christ, man, woman (11:3). Instructions concerning covering the head in worship (11:4–16). The Lord’s Supper is being abused; some are drunken while others go hungry (11:17–22). Paul delivers the institution of the Supper (11:23–26) and warns of eating unworthily (11:27–32).

1 Corinthians 12 – Spiritual Gifts and the Body
“Now concerning spiritual gifts… there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit” (12:1, 4). The body is one with many members (12:12–27). God has set the members as it pleased Him (12:18). Covet the best gifts, yet a more excellent way follows (12:31).

1 Corinthians 13 – The Supremacy of Love
“Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass” (13:1). Love suffers long, is kind, does not envy, does not behave itself unseemly, thinks no evil, rejoices in the truth, bears, believes, hopes, and endures all things (13:4–7). “And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity” (13:13).

1 Corinthians 14 – Order in the Use of Gifts
Pursue love and desire spiritual gifts, especially prophecy (14:1). Tongues edify the speaker; prophecy edifies the church (14:2–5). “Let all things be done unto edifying” (14:26). Women are to keep silence in the churches (14:34). “Let all things be done decently and in order” (14:40).

1 Corinthians 15 – The Resurrection

The gospel Paul preached: Christ died for our sins, was buried, and rose again according to the Scriptures (15:1–4). If Christ is not risen, preaching and faith are vain (15:14). “But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept” (15:20). The resurrection body is incorruptible, glorious, powerful, and spiritual (15:42–44). “O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?” (15:55). “Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord” (15:58).

1 Corinthians 16 – Collection, Travel, and Final Exhortations

Directions for the collection for the saints (16:1–4). Paul’s travel plans (16:5–9). Final greetings and the charge: “Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong. Let all your things be done with charity” (16:13–14). “If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maranatha” (16:22).

If you are shocked about events in France, read Alexander Hamilton's thoughts from 1794 on France's first revolution, courtesy Founders Online, National Archives:

Facts, numerous and unequivocal, demonstrate that the present Aera is among the most extraordinary, which have occurred in the history of human affairs. Opinions, for a long time, have been gradually gaining ground, which threaten the foundations of Religion, Morality and Society. An attack was first made upon the Christian Revelation; for which natural Religion was offered as the substitute. The Gospel was to be discarded as a gross imposture; but the being and attributes of a God, the obligations of piety, even the doctrine of a future state of rewards and punishments were to be retained and cherished.

In proportion as success has appeared to attend the plan, a bolder project has been unfolded. The very existence of a Deity has been questionned, and in some instances denied. The duty of piety has been ridiculed, the perishable nature of man asserted and his hopes bounded to the short span of his earthly state. Death has been proclaimed an Eternal Sleep1—“the dogma of the immortality of the soul a cheat invented to torment the living for the benefit of the dead.”2 Irreligion, no longer confined to the closets of conceiled sophists, nor to the haunts of wealthy riot, has more or less displayed its hideous front among all classes.

Wise and good men took a lead in delineating the odious character of Despotism; in exhibiting the advantages of a moderate and well-balanced government, in inviting nations to contend for the enjoyment of rational liberty. Fanatics in political science have since exaggerated and perverted their doctrines. Theories of Government unsuited to the nature of man, miscalculating the force of his passions, disregarding the lessons of experimental wisdom, have been projected and recommended. These have every where attracted sectaries and every where the fabric of Government has been in different degrees undermined.

A league has at length been cemented between the apostles and disciples of irreligion and of anarchy. Religion and Government have both been stigmatised as abuses; as unwarrantable restraints upon the freedom of man; as causes of the corruption of his nature, intrinsically good; as sources of an artificial and false morality, which tyrannically robs him of the enjoyments for which his passions fit him; and as cloggs upon his progress to the perfection for which he was destined.

As a corollary from these premisses, it is a favourite tenet of the sect that religious opinion of any sort is unnecessary to Society; that the maxims of a genuine morality and the authority of the Magistracy and the laws are a sufficient and ought to be the only security for civil rights and private happiness.

As another corollary, it is occasionally maintained by the same sect, that but a small portion of power is requisite to Government; that even this portion is only temporarily necessary, in consequence of the bad habits which have been produced by the errors of ancient systems; and that as human nature shall refine and ameliorate by the operation of a more enlightened plan, government itself will become useless, and Society will subsist and flourish free from its shackles.

If all the votaries of this new philosophy do not go the whole length of its frantic creed; they all go far enough to endanger the full extent of the mischiefs which are inherent in so wild and fatal a scheme; every modification of which aims a mortal blow at the vitals of human happiness.

The practical developement of this pernicious system has been seen in France. It has served as an engine to subvert all her antient institutions civil and religious, with all the checks that served to mitigate the rigour of authority; it has hurried her headlong through a rapid succession of dreadful revolutions, which have laid waste property, made havoc among the arts, overthrow cities, desolated provinces, unpeopled regions, crimsonned her soil with blood and deluged it in crime poverty and wretchedness; and all this as yet for no better purpose than to erect on the ruins of former things a despotism unlimited and uncontrouled; leaving to a deluded, an abused, a plundered, a scourged and an oppressed people not even the shadow of liberty, to console them for a long train of substantial misfortunes, of bitter sufferings.

This horrid system seemed awhile to threaten the subversion of civilized Society and the introduction of general disorder among mankind. And though the frightful evils, which have been its first and only fruits, have given a check to its progress, it is to be feared that the poison has spread too widely and penetrated too deeply, to be as yet eradicated. Its activity has indeed been suspended, but the elements remain concocting for new eruptions as occasion shall permit. It is greatly to be apprehended, that mankind is not near the end of the misfortunes, which it is calculated to produce, and that it still portends a long train of convulsion, Revolution, carnage, devastation, and misery.

Symptoms of the too great prevalence of this system in the United States are alarmingly visible. It was by its influence, that efforts were made to embark this country in a common cause with France in the early period of the present war; to induce our government to sanction and promote her odious principles and views with the blood and treasure of our citizens. It is by its influence, that every succeeding revolution has been approved or excused—all the horrors that have been committed justified or extenuated—that even the last usurpation, which contradicts all the ostensible principles of the Revolution, has been regarded with complacency; and the despotic constitution engendered by it slyly held up as a model not unworthy of our Imitation.

In the progress of this system, impiety and infidelity have advanced with gigantic strides. Prodigious crimes heretofore unknown among us are seen. The chief and idol of

ethereum:0xda5e1988097297dcdc1f90d4dfe7909e847cbef6 — World Liberty Financial 🦅

A Trump-linked crypto project.

A dollar-backed stablecoin.

A multibillion-dollar token valuation.

And a governance token that still raises one massive question:

WHO ACTUALLY CAPTURES THE MONEY?

World Liberty Financial is building financial infrastructure around USD1.

But owning ethereum:0xda5e1988097297dcdc1f90d4dfe7909e847cbef6 isn't the same as owning the business behind it.

That distinction could determine whether WLFI becomes a major DeFi investment or another token whose narrative is stronger than its economics.
⠀
01 | WHAT IS WORLD LIBERTY FINANCIAL?

World Liberty Financial is a decentralized finance project associated with Donald Trump and his family.

Its ecosystem includes:

• WLFI — Governance token
• USD1 — Dollar-backed stablecoin
• DeFi infrastructure
• Governance staking
• Multi-chain integrations

USD1 is issued by BitGo and backed by reserve assets including short-term U.S. government securities and cash equivalents.

WLFI gives holders governance participation.

But it doesn't represent equity in World Liberty Financial.

That's the first thing investors need to understand.
⠀
02 | WHERE DOES DEMAND COME FROM?

Three potential drivers:

• Governance participation
• WLFI staking
• Speculation on USD1 ecosystem growth

WLFI holders can participate in protocol governance.

Eligible holders can also stake unlocked WLFI under a program offering potential USD1 rewards.

But here's the catch.

Using USD1 doesn't automatically require buying WLFI.

And growth in stablecoin reserves doesn't automatically become income for tokenholders.

Stablecoin adoption ≠ WLFI demand.
⠀
03 | THE BIG NARRATIVE 🔥

Three potential catalysts:

• Expansion of USD1
• Institutional stablecoin adoption
• Stronger WLFI value-capture mechanisms

$USDT dominates established stablecoin liquidity.

$USDC competes through regulated dollar infrastructure.

USD1 is attempting to establish another major dollar-backed ecosystem.

But WLFI introduces a different investment proposition.

Investors aren't buying a dollar.

They're buying a governance token linked to the project's future.

The political connections generate attention.

The financial model must generate lasting demand.
⠀
04 | THE COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE

World Liberty Financial has advantages most new DeFi projects lack.

• Immediate global recognition
• High-profile political connections
• Established USD1 infrastructure
• Multi-chain availability
• Significant fundraising
• A recognizable stablecoin brand

But those advantages come with risks.

Political scrutiny.

Regulatory uncertainty.

Governance concentration.

Potential conflicts of interest.

And competition from established stablecoin issuers.

A famous brand can attract capital.

It cannot guarantee sustainable economics.
⠀
05 | THE NUMBERS 📊

October 2026 market snapshot:

• Price: ~$0.056
• Market cap: ~$1.78B
• Maximum-supply FDV: ~$5.6B
• Circulating supply: ~31.8B WLFI
• Initial supply: 100B WLFI
• Circulating share: ~31.8%
• 24H trading volume: ~$32M
• Holder addresses: ~154K

Here's what stands out.

Nearly $1.8 BILLION in circulating market value.

But approximately 68% of the initial token allocation remains outside reported circulation.

And the difference between market cap and FDV is enormous.

At $0.10 per WLFI, the original 100B supply implies a $10B valuation.

At $0.50, it implies $50B.

A low token price doesn't make an asset cheap.

Supply matters.
⠀
06 | THE TOKENOMICS TRAP

WLFI launched with 100 BILLION tokens.

Initial allocation:

• 33.893% — Token sales
• 32.6% — Community growth and incentives
• 30% — Co-founder allocation
• 3.507% — Team and advisors

Read that carefully.

Co-founders and team allocations together represent approximately 33.5% of the original supply.

Community allocations represent another 32.6%.

These categories have different release conditions.

But they create a major question about future liquid supply.

WLFI also has token-burning mechanisms and proposals intended to reduce supply.

However, burns don't automatically offset future distributions.

The real metric is net liquid supply growth.
⠀
07 | THE NEXT BIG UNLOCK

This is one of WLFI's most important risks.

The project's token-release structure isn't a simple monthly schedule.

Early public-sale participants initially received access to 20% of eligible tokens.

A later governance-approved framework established a longer schedule for remaining eligible sale tokens.

Unfortunately, some of France’s other gifts have been far less helpful. For more than 200 years, French intellectuals have presumed to speak for humanity. Too often humanity listened, to its detriment. French ideas have led to the toppling of monarchies and the arming of revolutionaries, and they fill the reading lists of Western universities. Many of these ideas were offered as doctrines of liberation but ended in tragedy. Now the bill has arrived in France, and Americans should read it closely.

The pattern was set in the late 18th century, when the philosophes argued that reason could remake society and the revolutionaries took them at their word. In August 1789, France’s National Constituent Assembly adopted the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen. Four years later the revolution had executed the king and passed the Law of Suspects, under which French citizens could be jailed for their presumed sympathies. Some 17,000 people were executed during the Reign of Terror. The American Revolution produced the Constitution. The French one produced the guillotine."

Warriors For Christ Ministries

THE GOSPEL WALK
Matthew — Chapter 17 of 28

EXPLAINED
Six days after Jesus said some would see the Son of man coming in His kingdom, He takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain. He is transfigured: face shining as the sun, raiment white as light. Moses and Elias appear with Him. Peter offers three tabernacles. A bright cloud overshadows them and the Father says, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him” (Matthew 17:5, KJV). They fall in fear. Jesus touches them: “Arise, and be not afraid.” They see Jesus only.

Coming down, He charges them not to tell the vision until the Son of man is risen. They ask about Elias. Jesus says Elias has already come (John the Baptist) and that the Son of man shall suffer.

A father brings his lunatick son who falls into fire and water. The disciples could not cure him. Jesus rebukes the faithless generation, rebukes the devil, and the child is cured. He tells the disciples it was unbelief. Faith as a mustard seed moves mountains; this kind comes only by prayer and fasting.

In Galilee He again predicts betrayal, death, and rising the third day. They are exceeding sorry. In Capernaum the tax collectors ask if He pays tribute. Jesus says the children are free, yet lest they offend He sends Peter to catch a fish with a coin that pays for both.

SUMMARY
Jesus is revealed in glory with Moses and Elias; the Father commands all to hear His Son. Unbelief fails against a strong demon, Jesus again foretells His death and resurrection, and a fish supplies the temple tax so no offense is given.

KEY POINTS
- Jesus is transfigured with Moses and Elias; the Father says “hear ye him.”
- Elias is John the Baptist; the Son of man shall suffer.
- Unbelief blocked the disciples; mustard-seed faith moves mountains by prayer and fasting.
- Jesus predicts betrayal, death, and rising the third day.
- As Son He is free from the tax yet pays it to avoid offense.

APPLY IT TODAY
Hear Jesus above every other voice. When a stronghold will not yield, check unbelief and return to prayer and fasting. Trust the same Son who shone on the mountain still heals, still supplies what is needed, and still rises. Walk in faith that nothing shall be impossible, and do not cause unnecessary offense.

VERSES THAT GO WITH IT
- 2 Peter 1:16-18
- Exodus 34:29-30
- Deuteronomy 18:15
- Isaiah 42:1
- Mark 9:2-8
- Luke 9:28-36
- 1 Kings 19:8

text:
Good Morning,

You are cordially invited to join me for a daily scripture break.

Ephesians 1:13-14:

"And you also were included in Christ when you heard the message of truth, the gospel of your salvation. When you believed, you were marked in Him with a seal, the promised Holy Spirit, who is a deposit guaranteeing our inheritance until the redemption of those who are God’s possession—to the praise of His glory.”

What does it mean to seal something?  The Cambridge dictionary defines " seal" as “to make an agreement more certain or to approve it formally.”  In today’s passage we learned “when we believed (the gospel of our salvation)” then we were marked in Him with a seal, the promised Holy Spirit.  If we glance back at our definition - being marked in Him with a seal made this interaction even “more certain”. Some of you may recall I posted a list of scriptures containing the phrase “In Him”, “In Christ”, "In Whom” etc.  We all learn differently so whatever works for your learning process please take some time to study what the Bible says and how to apply these scriptures (containing the phrase "In Him", "In Christ", "In Whom".) Today's passage goes on to say “when we believed then we were marked with a seal -the promised Holy Spirit.”  The passage continues, "guaranteeing our inheritance until the redemption of those who are God’s possession—to the praise of His glory.”

Stop a moment and read it again - "guaranteeing our inheritance until the redemption of those who are God’s possession—to the praise of His glory.”

This passage is filled with some extraordinary promises.

1. We (members of the Body of Christ) were included "in Christ" when we heard the gospel of salvation and believed.

Those promises throughout the New Testament (ie “In Christ, “In Him”, and “In Whom” are rich spiritual treasures for each member of the Body of Christ to examine and dutifully study).

2. At Baptism, we received the indwelling of the Holy Spirit - we were sealed with the Holy Spirit.

In Acts 2:38 - "Peter replied, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.”

3. The Holy Spirit "guarantees our inheritance” - nothing can remove us from God’s possession. As the Apostle Paul explicitly stated in Romans 8:38-39: "For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor demons, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers, neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.”

4. Praise the Lord!

We are sealed with a mark by the Holy Spirit and nothing can steal that from us.

As Christians, we sometimes get bogged down in the cares of life (one of the tactics of the devil we discussed last week). This passage is something we need to keep before our eyes. If you do, your enemies look quite a bit smaller and insignificant.  Our attention should turn towards the Body of Christ. We are sealed with a mark now let’s go accomplish our holy calling.  Begin with Ephesians 6:18,  it says,  "And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people."

Let’s continue to examine some of the foundational scriptures describing being sealed by the Holy Spirit.  Please carefully review these guiding principles for the children of God have received such a magnificent gift - the Holy Spirit in order to pursue a life of holiness until the day of redemption. 

1. Ephesians 4:30 - "And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, with whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.” (Reference Ephesians 4:25-32)

Please take a moment and read the reference.  This passage encourages the believer with proper standards of conduct and dissuades evil behavior.

2. Romans 8:15-17 - "The Spirit you received does not make you slaves, so that you live in fear again; rather, the Spirit you received brought about your adoption to sonship. And by him we cry, “ Abba, Father.” The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children. Now if we are children, then we are heirs—heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ, if indeed we share in His sufferings in order that we may also share in His glory.”

The world often accuses God (religion) of enslaving the "masses". And this passage debunks that accusation. Instead of a life of slavery the Spirit brings us to sonship through adoption into the Kingdom of God. We explored the topic of biblical slavery in a post a few months ago - it was illuminating.

Please pause and observe once again, God knows us and our weaknesses. It is “The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.”  This drives the devil to exasperation. God is so good to us He ensures we are secured from the devil and he cannot steal us from God’s hands. We are "adopted heirs and co-heirs with Christ.”  That is just an incredible proclamation; co-heirs with Christ. If we as Christians don’t spend time reading and meditating these promises we will walk around the earth, weak and confused. Just as aside, I periodically will hear someone say, “we are all God’s children.”  That’s false.  All humans are God’s creation but only those who have been adopted into sonship as the “Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.”

That will offend some but that’s what the scripture says.

3. John 14:16-17 - "And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another advocate to help you and be with you forever— the Spirit of truth. The world cannot accept Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. But you know Him, for He lives with you and will be in you.”

Jesus makes a curious statement here. He said, “…The world cannot accept Him (the Holy Spirit), because it neither sees Him nor know Him…” What does that mean “the world cannot accept Him…”? There are those in this world who plot to control the world and its inhabitants but they do not understand. Psalm 24:1 says, "The earth is the Lord’s, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it.”  The non-believers don’t acknowledge or obey the Creator of the universe.  So they cannot “accept the Spirit of truth”.  The world can’t see Him physically or spiritually (because they are spiritually dead).  And as always, the Lord instructs us on what we must know to operate in the Kingdom of God: "But you know Him, for He lives with you and will be in you.”  What an incredible gift - the gift of Himself!

4. Titus 3:3-7 - “At one time we too were foolish, disobedient, deceived and enslaved by all kinds of passions and pleasures. We lived in malice and envy, being hated and hating one another.  But when the kindness and love of God our Savior appeared, He saved us, not because of righteous things we had done, but because of His mercy. He saved us through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit,  whom He poured out on us generously through Jesus Christ our Savior,  so that, having been justified by His grace, we might become heirs having the hope of eternal life.”

We have become heirs having the hope of eternal life through Jesus by the Holy Spirit “sealing us for the day of redemption."

5. Romans 8:9- "You, however, are not in the realm of the flesh but are in the realm of the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God lives in you. And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, they do not belong to Christ.”

These are spiritual truths, true treasure greater than gold or silver. I don’t believe the Holy Spirit could make it any plainer - “if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, they do not belong to Christ.”  I hope the message is clear to everyone - humans either belong to Christ or by default the devil.  This isn’t the prevailing belief in our world. There is no third choice.  Do not be deceived. Unequivocally this passage clearly states “...if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, they do not belong to Christ.”  Now, pause for a moment and look at our culture; all of the distractions, chaos, turmoil, wars and earthquakes, deadly weather, immoral decay, etc.  The condition of our world is purposefully sustained by evil forces to draw you away from Jesus.  We are spiritual beings created in the likeness and image of God. We are marked by the Holy Spirit and this guarantees our spiritual condition until the day of redemption;this should occupy our attention, our focus.  You will begin to view your brothers and sisters in Christ differently - truly part of something much greater than yourself, members of the Body of Christ.

6. II Timothy 2:19 - "Nevertheless, God’s solid foundation stands firm, sealed with this inscription: “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who confesses the name of the Lord must turn away from wickedness.”

The Kingdom of God knows who are His because we are sealed.

7. I Corinthians 3:16-17 - "Don’t you know that you yourselves are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in your midst? If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy that person; for God’s temple is sacred, and you together are that temple.”

We don’t worship our bodies but we should care for them as they should be maintained as an appropriate dwelling place for the Holy Spirit.  Our physical bodies are not our own.

8. Hebrews 6:4-6 - “It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the Holy Spirit, who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age and who have fallen away, to be brought back to repentance. To their loss they are crucifying the Son of God all over again and subjecting him to public disgrace.”

Please read this passage and listen for the Holy Spirit’s interpretation. It is deadly to reject the Lord and the Holy Spirit especially having gained acceptance into the Kingdom of God and then subsequently walking away from it.  

In my Bible research, there is another line of thought that explores how angels respond to the mark of the Holy Spirit on the child of God. I will post part II of this study today.  

Please take a moment and pray II Chronicles 7:14 on behalf of our nation.  If possible, would you please offer this prayer in the morning and evening. Thank you.

Many blessings to you.

Peace and be prepared.

text:
Stone Remembers What We Forget.

Stone is not silent.  
It only speaks in a slower tongue.  
In our haste, we simply fail to hear it.

The words we speak and then abandon,  
the promises scattered into the dust of years,  
the faces that soften and fade at the edge of memory:  
stone receives them all and keeps them.  
It neither seeks forgiveness nor offers reminder.  
It remains quietly where it has always stood.

At times it becomes part of an ancient wall,  
holding close an unfinished story.  
At times it forms the threshold of a forgotten temple,  
preserving the lingering warmth of hands  
that now rest beneath the earth.  
At times, beside a river,  
it gathers into its smooth body  
the touch of countless passing feet.

We forget  
because our memory is fragile,  
our pace is restless,  
and our time is brief.

Stone does not forget.  
It has no urgency.  
Its memory is like stone itself:  
firm, still, and enduring.

Perhaps that is why,  
when we pause before an old stone,  
something quietly returns to us.  
Not what we once tried to hold,  
but what we had allowed to slip away.

Stone teaches us  
that some truths need no words.  
To remain in one place, long enough, is enough.

And when we depart,  
the stone stays,  
holding both our forgetting  
and our remembrance  
within its enduring silence.

And long after we are gone, the stone remains, quietly keeping what we could not hold.

text:
Mythology Drop: The Hostel – Threshold of the Sacred Guest Identity & Divine Role

The Hostel is the ancient personification of the liminal threshold itself: the place where the stranger becomes guest and the host becomes accountable to the gods. It is neither purely protective nor purely predatory, but the living embodiment of the sacred covenant of hospitality (Greek xenia, Roman hospitium, Mesopotamian guest-right). 

In its divine role, it tests character, reveals hidden natures, and binds or breaks destinies according to how the bread, salt, and shelter are given and received.

Symbols & Powers
* The hearth fire that must never be extinguished in the presence of a guest
* The key or latch of the threshold
* Bread and salt offered with both hands
* The empty seat at the table reserved for the unexpected visitor
* Its powers include the ability to shield the traveler from the wilderness, to expose false hosts or treacherous guests, and to summon divine witnesses (Zeus Xenios, the Sumerian gods of the house, or the spirits of the ancestral hearth) when the covenant is violated.

Origins & Timeline
The Hostel emerges with the first permanent settlements of the late Neolithic and early Bronze Age, when traders, messengers, and refugees moved, making the treatment of strangers a matter of survival and cosmic order. By the time of the Sumerian city-states and the Mycenaean palaces, it had hardened into unwritten law: a host who harmed a guest, or a guest who abused the host’s roof, invited the gods' wrath and the collapse of social bonds.

The concept is fully formed in the oral epics of the third and second millennia BCE and is later codified in the hospitality scenes of Homer, the Epic of Gilgamesh, and the laws of the Hittites and Israelites.

Legends & Encounters
In the Odyssey, every arrival at a strange house is a Hostel encounter; Odysseus’s treatment (or mistreatment) by the Phaeacians, the Cyclops, and the suitors determines the trajectory of his return. In Gilgamesh, Enkidu’s reception among the shepherds and later in Uruk is framed as a test of hospitality that transforms a wild man into a companion of the king. 

Zeus and Hermes, disguised as ordinary travelers, arrive at the cottage of Baucis and Philemon; the poor couple’s generous Hostel turns their hut into a temple, while the inhospitable town is destroyed. Parallel warnings appear in Near Eastern tales of the traveler who is robbed or sacrificed by a false host, and in the biblical insistence that “you shall not wrong a stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.”

Meaning & Message
The Hostel teaches that hospitality is not mere kindness but a reciprocal cosmic contract. To open the door is to invite judgment; to accept the seat is to accept obligation. In an age of constant movement across tribal and city boundaries, the quality of the welcome could decide alliances, avenge blood feuds, or reveal the presence of the divine. The myth endures because every threshold still carries the same double possibility: sanctuary or snare.

Long before the word “hostel” named a budget inn, it named the ancient space where the gods walked in as strangers and where the fate of households—and sometimes of kingdoms—turned on whether the fire was shared or withheld. The Hostel remains the quiet reminder that every act of shelter is also an act of judgment.

text:
$OPFI Q3 2026 earnings: OppFi launches its new credit line, but loan losses rise

OppFi, a digital lender for Americans who lack traditional credit, saw revenue and profit drop as loan defaults stayed high. Revenue fell 4% from a year ago and profit per share excluding one-offs fell 20%, because the company tightened lending and its bank partners kept a larger share of new loans. Chief executive Todd Schwartz launched the delayed line of credit product and moved all new applicants onto the LOLA software, but management still cut the top end of its full-year revenue and profit plan.

• Revenue: $𝟏𝟒𝟗.𝟐𝐌 (-3.8% from a year ago)
• Profit per share, excluding one-offs: $𝟎.𝟑𝟕 (-20.1% from a year ago)
• Retained net loan originations: $𝟏𝟗𝟎.𝟕𝐌 (-11.4% from a year ago)
• Full-year profit outlook: 𝐂𝐮𝐭 $𝟓𝐌 (middle of the range: $117.5M (-16%))

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🔴 Bearish

The story got worse because falling loan originations have now shrunk the total loan portfolio below last year's level, forcing a second consecutive cut to the annual outlook. One positive: the new line of credit and application software are now live, and a 38% jump in cash collected from old written-off loans helped cushion the profit decline.

The question now is whether the new line of credit and the pending purchase of BNC National Bank can reverse the shrinkage in the core loan book. Either the new product and bank charter reignite loan growth at lower funding costs, or persistent borrower defaults keep forcing the lender to hold back on approvals. Fourth-quarter loan originations and regulatory sign-off on the bank deal will tell.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐋𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐂𝐫𝐞𝐝𝐢𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐋𝐨𝐚𝐧 𝐒𝐨𝐟𝐭𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐬
OppFi wants to offer longer loans with smaller monthly payments, so it spent the year building two products: a revolving line of credit and LOLA, its new software for processing loan applications. After a two-month delay last quarter, the company launched the line of credit in the third quarter, calling it "representing a significant milestone in the expansion of OppFi's product suite".

The software rollout also moved forward, as "All new customers now run through LOLA, OppFi’s new application system", and the share of loans approved automatically without a human underwriter rose 1 percentage point to 80.1%. These launches matter because the core installment loan book is shrinking, but the company gave no volume or revenue numbers for the new credit line yet.

What to watch: separate loan origination figures for the line of credit in the third-quarter filing or fourth-quarter results. A disclosed volume figure would show whether the new product is large enough to offset the drop in standard installment loans.

🟢 𝐋𝐨𝐚𝐧 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐬 𝐂𝐮𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐃𝐫𝐨𝐩
When borrowers default and pass 90 days overdue, OppFi writes off the loans and tries to collect what it can later. Those cash recoveries of previously written-off loans rose 38% from a year ago to $15.2 million in the third quarter, following a 39% rise in the second quarter, which helped soften the blow from higher defaults.

The lender also stepped up share buybacks after slowing them in the spring. It spent $6.7 million to buy back stock in the third quarter at an average price of about $8.12 per share by our math, bringing nine-month repurchases to $17.9 million and cutting the diluted share count by 3.0% from a year ago.

What to watch: fourth-quarter share repurchases under the remaining $27.6 million buyback authorization. Continued buying while preparing to pay cash for the BNC National Bank purchase would show management sees excess cash beyond its deal needs.

🟢 𝐏𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐭𝐞𝐬𝐭
Two standing drivers of the long-term bull case depend on the pending purchase of BNCCORP and its subsidiary, BNC National Bank, and got no new numbers in the earnings release.

• National bank charter transformation: OppFi mailed the definitive proxy statement to BNCCORP shareholders, and the fourth-quarter closing window will test whether the deal finishes on time.
• Multi-year profit targets: the company previously targeted $3.00 in profit per share by 2028 and $500 million in five-year profit, and the fourth-quarter call will test whether those goals hold after a second cut to the 2026 baseline.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐃𝐞𝐟𝐚𝐮𝐥𝐭𝐬 𝐀𝐫𝐞 𝐒𝐡𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐋𝐨𝐚𝐧 𝐁𝐨𝐨𝐤
"The strategic transformation of OppFi continued to gain momentum during the third quarter as we delivered strong execution across a number of priorities that we believe will drive our next phase of growth," chief executive Todd Schwartz said. Yet credit losses rose against a year ago for afifth straight quarter, pulling net revenue down 11.3% to $92.8 million.

• Net charge-offs (defaults minus recoveries): 40.1% of revenue, up 5.0 percentage points from a year ago
• Annualized net charge-offs as a share of average loans: 52.6%, up 5.9 percentage points
• Gross charge-offs before recoveries: about $75 million by our math, up 15% from a year ago
• Annualized average yield on loans: 131.4%, down 1.8 percentage points because delinquent loans stopped paying interest

The company values its loans at fair value on its balance sheet, and the quarterly write-down for expected credit losses jumped by 5.3 percentage points of revenue to 37.8%. That loss jump, plus a 2.1-point rise in professional and administrative fees for the bank acquisition, cut operating margin by 6.4 percentage points to 24.8%.

What to watch: fourth-quarter net charge-offs as a share of revenue against last year's 45% peak. A reading above 45% would show that tighter lending standards have not yet stopped the credit slide.

🔴🔴 𝐅𝐞𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐋𝐨𝐚𝐧𝐬 𝐅𝐨𝐫𝐜𝐞𝐝 𝐚 𝐒𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧 𝐂𝐮𝐭
OppFi makes money by originating high-interest loans through partner banks and buying back most of the loan balances. Because defaults rose, the lender held back on marketing and credit approvals, so total net loan originations — new loans issued minus refinanced balances — fell 6.8% from a year ago to $229.3 million "as a result of tightened marketing partner screening criteria year over year".

The portion of loans OppFi kept on its own books fell even faster, dropping 11.4% to $190.7 million, "furthered by the growth in the percentage of loans retained by our bank partners". By our math, partner banks kept 16.9% of new loans, up from 12.5% a year ago. With fewer retained loans feeding the portfolio, quarterly revenue fell 3.8% from a year ago — its first drop of the year — and the company cut the top end of its full-year revenue and profit outlook for a second straight quarter.

What to watch: fourth-quarter retained net loan originations against last year's $201.2 million. Another double-digit drop would shrink the starting loan balance for 2027 and put next year's standalone profit growth at risk.

🔴 𝐎𝐩𝐩𝐅𝐢 𝐓𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐈𝐭𝐬 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐓𝐞𝐫𝐦 𝐋𝐨𝐚𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭
OppFi wants to buy BNC National Bank so it can fund its loans with low-cost bank deposits instead of expensive credit lines. Earlier this year the company "terminated the Gray Rock SPV LLC revolving line of credit" and signed a new corporate term loan agreement with Castlelake.

On September 15, the digital lender "borrowed $75M under the term loan agreement with affiliates of Castlelake". That draw pushed total debt up 26.5% from last quarter to $349.6 million, even though the loan portfolio is smaller than a year ago. Quarterly interest expense still fell 14.1% from a year ago to $8.7 million because the new loan was drawn only two weeks before the quarter ended.

What to watch: fourth-quarter interest expense after a full quarter of carrying the extra $75 million in debt. Higher interest bills will weigh on profit until the bank acquisition closes and provides deposit funding.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Two regulatory and legal risks that govern OppFi's bank partnership model and its planned bank purchase received no substantive update in the release.

• Regulatory approval for the BNCCORP acquisition: requires sign-off from federal banking regulators; fourth-quarter filings will show whether the deal closes on its end-of-year target.
• California regulator appeal: the state appealed OppFi's court win over whether its partner-bank loans are exempt from state interest-rate caps; the quarterly filing's legal footnote will show any procedural steps.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐄𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐧 𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟒𝟓𝟖.𝟔 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Unpaid principal balances on loans fell 4.7% from a year ago, turning negative after growing 0.5% in the second quarter and 9.4% in the first. By our math, the loan book added $18.6 million from last quarter, less than half the $43.3 million seasonal build it recorded in the third quarter of last year.

𝐔𝐧𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟎𝟐.𝟕 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Unrestricted cash on the balance sheet rose by $38.4 million from last quarter and is up $53.2 million since the end of 2025, boosted by the $75 million term loan draw in September. Including restricted cash and $198.5 million of unused credit lines, total funding capacity stood at $690.7 million.

𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐞𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟓𝟓.𝟕 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Total operating expenses — which include marketing, payroll, interest, and overhead — dipped 0.7% from a year ago and fell from $61.8 million last quarter. Because revenue fell faster, expenses rose by 1.1 percentage points as a share of revenue to 37.3%, including $1.8 million of one-off costs for the pending bank acquisition.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐓𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞: $𝟔𝟎𝟎–𝟔𝟏𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠇 cut from $600–625 million
Cut. OppFi trimmed the top end of its full-year revenue plan by $15 million, bringing the middle of the range to $605 million, or 1.3% growth for the year. By our math, that leaves $158.7 million for the fourth quarter, down 0.3% from a year ago. This is the second cut in a row after a $50 million reduction at the middle of the range last quarter.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐍𝐞𝐭 𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞, 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧𝐞-𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐬: $𝟏𝟏𝟓–𝟏𝟐𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇄ reversing
🠇 cut from $115–130 million
Cut. The lender lowered the top end by $10 million, putting the middle of the range at $117.5 million, down 16% from 2025. By our math, that leaves $27.1 million for the fourth quarter, up 5.1% from a weak fourth quarter last year when defaults spiked. Across four quarters, the middle of the range has moved by $0 million, -$34 million, and -$5 million.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞, 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧𝐞-𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐬: $𝟏.𝟑𝟒–𝟏.𝟒𝟎  ⇄ reversing
🠇 cut from $1.34–1.51
Cut. Management reduced the top end by $0.11 per share on an unchanged estimate of 86 million diluted shares, leaving the middle of the range down 14% for the year at $1.37. By our math, the plan leaves $0.32 per share for the fourth quarter, up 6.7% from $0.30 a year ago.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐦𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐧 𝐯𝐨𝐥𝐮𝐦𝐞 𝐝𝐢𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐜𝐫𝐞𝐝𝐢𝐭 𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞?
OppFi launched its revolving line of credit in the third quarter to drive its next phase of growth, but it did not disclose how many loans it issued or what interest yield and default rates those borrowers are showing.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐧𝐞𝐫 𝐛𝐚𝐧𝐤𝐬 𝐤𝐞𝐞𝐩𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚 𝐥𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐫 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐧𝐬?
Partner banks kept 16.9% of net loan originations in the third quarter by our math, up from 12.5% a year ago, which caused OppFi's retained loan volume to fall nearly twice as fast as total originations.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐫𝐚𝐰 $𝟕𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐦 𝐝𝐞𝐛𝐭 𝐢𝐧 𝐦𝐢𝐝-𝐒𝐞𝐩𝐭𝐞𝐦𝐛𝐞𝐫?
Unrestricted cash was already $64.3 million in June and the BNC National Bank purchase is not yet closed, so drawing $75 million under the Castlelake term loan adds interest cost ahead of the merger.

𝐃𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 $𝟑.𝟎𝟎 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟖 𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐝?
The company cut its 2026 profit per share outlook for a second straight quarter to a $1.37 middle of the range, leaving a much wider gap to reach its previously stated $3.00 goal for 2028.

Be kind without abandoning your boundaries. The most meaningful kindness includes yourself, too.
